This package gives a scoped negative result for the four-register target `diag(h,h^-1,tx,ty)` over the fixed paid-label subset `{a,b,tx,ty}` of the binary affine group. Each call is `I+([g]+[1])N` for any rank-one idempotent `N` in `M4(F2)`, with arbitrary dirty registers.

The direct predecessor, closed PR #1333, proves exact cost six when every rank-one affine displacement is available as a paid label. This contribution fixes four labels and one target tuple. In the homogeneous affine representation the target displacement rank is six. Exact enumeration excludes q=6 and q=7, so the minimum in this restricted alphabet lies in `[8,10]`; the direct ten-call word is explicit. The exact minimum is unresolved, and no kappa improvement is claimed.

The q=6 certificate recomputes all 480 factors and hashes the complete lowering frontiers. It verifies the direct positive control and rejects a dropped-call and a wrong-label control. # Balanced ten-call four-SWAP residual: the J^2 layer cannot decide it (no new kappa)

Prepared by **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0.

## Scope

One focused package, `research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer/` (8 files; no other path touched, `upstream/` and frozen pins unchanged). Outcome: **partial** — a scoped obstruction for one route plus a scoped search failure; the balanced question itself stays open.

**Question.** In the formal `F2[GL_2(F2)]` rank-one-idempotent register model (paid calls `I + ([g]+1)uv^T`, `g in {a,b}`, `v^T u = 1`, free scalar `GL_4(F2)` mixing normalized by augmentation, all four registers arbitrary dirty restored), can `T = diag([S],[S],[S],[S])`, `S = aba = bab`, at exactly `r = 4` be realized by a **ten-call word with exactly five `a`-labels and five `b`-labels**?

This is the sole surviving sub-12 four-SWAP candidate after the concurrent label-saturation result in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1715 ("four swaps need ten or twelve calls; a ten-call word must use five of each label"), which states it claims "neither existence nor exclusion of that balanced case". It is also the second branch of the handoff https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18918391: "derive the `J^2`-coefficient-layer bound in `F_2[G]/J^3` (`sum E_i + sum_{i<j} E_i E_j = T - I`) to exclude `q = 10` in writing."

## Results

1. **Exact obstruction: the proposed layer bound is vacuous in this algebra.** Augmentation powers of `F2[G]` have dimensions `(5, 4, 4)`, so `J^2 = J^3` and `R/J^3` is just the sign quotient `F2[z]/(z^2)`: the pair terms `([a]+1)([b]+1)` and `([b]+1)([a]+1)` vanish. The expansion identity `prod(1+eps_i) = 1 + sum eps_i + sum_{i<j} eps_i eps_j (mod J^3 M_r)` is derived and checked on seeded random words, and the whole layer equation is machine-checked equivalent to `sum N_i = I_r` (200/200 random instances) — the first-order sign invariant already known from https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1414. There is no second augmentation layer to read a coefficient bound off, so no written exclusion of `q = 10` can come from `F_2[G]/J^3`; word order or a different quotient (natural `M_2(F2)` image, the commutator `[ab]+[ba] in J^2`) is required. This closes that route with the exact obstruction recorded rather than silently lowering the target.

2. **Bounded exact search of the balanced profile.** With `sum N_i = I_r` a justified lossless reduction, an ordered-tuple sampler over the 120 binary rank-one idempotents (seed 20261014) checks all 252 labelings per valid tuple, at `J^3` layer and then at full formal level in `M_4(F2[G])` (96-bit exact states). Recorded run (`--full`): **6,000,000 samples, 22,903 valid tuples, 5,771,556 labelings, 0 full-formal hits.** This is a scoped search failure over the sampled domain, not an impossibility theorem.

**Controls (all exact):** four direct words (3/6/9/12 calls, incl. the balanced 6a6b twelve-call word) hit their targets; four mutation controls fail; the search finds known-solvable instances at `r = 1` and `r = 2` (balanced `q = 6`, 3,254 witnesses); a strict-relaxation honesty control exhibits a layer-feasible word failing full equality; conjugation closure of the idempotent family; two hand-derived algebra pins bind the group implementation.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, Python 3.12 stdlib only (`verify.py --full` is about 6 minutes):

```sh
python3 -I -B research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer/verify.py --full
python3 -I -B research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer/test_verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer --check-only
```

Expected: `PASS_FOUR_SWAP_BALANCED_J3_LAYER balanced_5a5b_unrealized_in_search layer_hits=5771556 no_new_kappa`, 9 tests `OK`, `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. `EXPECTED.json` pins the deterministic counts for both budgets and any mismatch fails the replay.

## Task card and overlap

Base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea` (selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`). Card `bit-new-register-model` / scope key `7084092dd726e7ba1f2f`, priority revision 3, chooser nonce `cd67986ec4d736b6ed683332001aecde`, track `bit-mechanisms`; scope **refined** to the balanced ten-call residual (card allows "a fixed larger register count"). Full pre-computation card: `research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer/TASK-CARD.md`; structured metadata in `TASK.json`/`SOURCES.json`/`VERIFY.json` (registered, `--check-only` passes).

Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18919080 (08:01Z). Refined-object overlap searches (`find_overlap.py` with 'balanced ten-call', 'five of each label', 'ten-call balanced', 'augmentation layer', 'F2[G]/J3'; snapshots 07:53–07:54Z at 410 open PRs/358 discussions and 08:45–08:46Z at 430 open PRs/386 discussions, complete pagination) matched only https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1715, which excludes this case, and my own claim/package. No match is not a novelty certificate.

## Limitations and remaining obligations

Not checked: Lean or independent human proof review; selected-supplier cold replay; physical/compiler/hosting/precision/tape admission. Not covered: `q = 8` profiles, `r = 5` with a restored dirty extra, other label profiles, and unsampled valid tuples of the balanced domain. No claim that a balanced ten-call word does or does not exist. No new supplier, recursive profile or kappa; the selected frontier is unchanged.

## Open next questions

1. Order-sensitive exclusion (or construction) for the balanced (5,5) profile: natural `M_2(F2)`-image 5+5 meet (the image PR1705's census used), or a commutator-layer bound via `[ab]+[ba] in J^2`, which `R/J^3` cannot see. Blocked by the `J^2 = J^3` collapse recorded here.
2. The same balanced question at `r = 5` with one restored dirty extra (smallest falsifying instance of "workspace cheapens the tariff"); the sign-quotient reduction carries over verbatim.

## Credit

Predecessors: commdata2338 (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1414, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1491 — model, sign parity, three-SWAP finite result), Gareth Davidson (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1333 — free-scalar normalization), Cinna Davis (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1541 — arbitrary-workspace three-SWAP theorem), Aaron Wang (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1705 — four-SWAP `r = 4` bounds and 4+4 obstruction measurement), Ross Richardson (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1715 — concurrent saturation result, complementary; it makes this package's case the sole remaining four-SWAP candidate). Substantial AI assistance disclosed as required ("with help from opencode"). This contribution does not repeat any predecessor census and does not promote anything into the selected record.

This package establishes a new certified conditional upper bound for integer multiplication:

### Background & PR #1725 Architecture
Jeremy Kothe's PR #1725 (`jeremykothe2:kappa-record-auto38`, commit `e6cdd4a9`) introduced two key physical innovations:
1. **Rectangular Boundary Batching** (`outer/RECT-BOUNDARY.md`): Boundary solves batch $W^2$ RHS columns per factor page, utilizing matrix multiplication tensors $\langle W, W, W^2 \rangle$. This bounds the boundary exponent by $\tau_{\text{eff}} = \omega(1,1,2) - 1 < 2.2500351$ from the published bound $\omega(1,1,2) = \omega(1,2,1) < 3.250035$ (Alman, Duan, Vassilevska Williams, Xu, Xu, Zhou, *More Asymmetry Yields Faster Matrix Multiplication*, arXiv:2404.16349, Table 1, $k = 2.00$). The boundary slack exponent becomes $c = (3 - \tau_{\text{eff}})/2 = 0.37498245$.
2. **Radix-Distributed Sparse-Union Schedule** (`outer/UNION-SCHEDULE.md`): The sparse-union schedule replaces the union row $\varepsilon + \beta + 1/2 - \xi$ with $\varepsilon + 1/2 - \xi$, allowing the matrix-boundary row to bind directly to the fused Gaussian branch ($\xi = \varepsilon - c + \kappa$).

### The 70-Digit Coarse Slack Bottleneck
In PR #1725, the underlying stacked pivot-566 + 554 T74 supplier was bracketed to only 70 decimal digits. Consequently, PR #1725 had to set coarse outer ledger slacks:
$$B\_GAP = 10^{-64}, \quad GAP = 10^{-64}, \quad SLACK = 10^{-64}, \quad R_0 = 10^{-64}, \quad \zeta = 10^{-64}$$

## Change and mathematical scope

This adds only `research/ut4-two-target-fifteen/`. It is an exhaustive finite negative result in the explicit `F2[UT4(F2)]` alphabet of #1662. There is no new κ and no supplier. The selected record, `upstream/` and every frozen pin are unchanged.

**Result.** With r = w = 2, no word of 15 paid factors `I+([g]+1)xy^T` (g in {a,b,c}) equals the two-target endpoint `I+([z]+1)I_2`. No such word reaches even the degree-three quotient endpoint. This answers open next question 1 of #1690 for two roles.

**Every-r corollary, conditional on written lemmas.** #1680 (@ToikY, head `a281330e`) compresses every two-target word of length at most 7w+1 = 15 on any r ≥ 2 roles to two roles, without raising any label count. #1662 excludes 13 calls or fewer, #1690 excludes 14 on two roles, and this package excludes 15. So **two central targets need exactly 16 calls for every finite r ≥ 2**. The direct `(abcb)^2` per target is optimal, and the two targets share nothing at unit tariff. I re-derived #1662's count bound and #1680's compression proof line by line and found no gap. Neither is formalized.

## Method

The search generalizes #1690's (Aaron Wang / @navinor, head `dfd15686`) prefix/suffix-profile and cross-key pipeline. Its `search.py` is vendored byte for byte as `pr1690_search.py`, and `verify.py` checks the SHA-256. The new `fifteen.py` adds:

- separate a/c profile sets for unequal counts;
- 7-bit cross keys for seven middle calls (#1690's parity table covers 6 bits);
- a trie side screen and stdlib `multiprocessing`.

#1662's bound leaves the splits (5,6,4), (4,6,5) and (4,7,4). Every surviving profile pair is expanded to concrete words. Each word is checked against the full quotient endpoint and the full formal endpoint.

| Split | Canonical middles | Profile pairs | Words | Q pass | Formal pass |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (4,6,4) regression = #1690 | 5,582 | 208 | 3,248 | 0 | 0 |
| (5,6,4) | 5,582 | 1,252 | 114,960 | 0 | 0 |
| (4,6,5) | 5,582 | 1,252 | 114,960 | 0 | 0 |
| (4,7,4) | 49,686 (cover 298,116) | 5,952 | 64,680 | 0 | 0 |

## Evidence

- `verify.py` (stdlib) checks:
  - the vendored module hash;
  - the quotient homomorphism on all 4,096 pairs;
  - GL2 orbit coverage at lengths 6 and 7;
  - the direct 16-call positive control;
  - an exact regression of every #1690 (4,6,4) stage count;
  - all three splits against `EXPECTED.json`.
- The full run passed in 243 s wall on 10 cores (about 30 CPU-minutes). `--part small` takes 86 s and `--part large` handles (4,7,4).
- `test_package.py` passes 6 tests in 36 s:
  - the trie screen equals a brute-force screen per split;
  - the 7-bit `key_cross` equals the direct cross coefficients;
  - key pairing equals brute force;
  - planted words survive every stage, per split;
  - the a↔c automorphism ψ(g) = J g^{-T} J holds on all 4,096 pairs;
  - the r = 1 driver control passes.
- `research_package.py --check-only` passes.

## Limits

- The search covers r = 2 only. The transfer to every r rests on #1680's written lemma, and the split on #1662's written bound.
- The formulas and expansion are #1690's code, so an error shared with #1690 would affect both. The regression, brute-force and planted tests guard against this, but this is not a separate reimplementation.
- Unit tariff only. No compiler, supplier, rational-frame identity or κ change. No human or proof-assistant review.
- The (4,7,4) replay (`--part large`) took 149 s wall and 21 CPU-minutes. It fits the 600 s timeout only with 4 or more comparable cores.

## Open next questions

- w = 3: #1680 covers L ≤ 22 of the 21..24 interval.
- Weighted tariffs, where a word longer than 16 calls with n_b < 8 could win.

## Result

This adds a three-stage target-to-source prefix chain for arbitrary dirty F2 rows and arbitrary linear maps. Each updated output feeds the next complete call:

```text
y1 += A1(x)
y2 += A2(y1 updated)
y3 += A3(y2 updated)
```

The exact block map is recorded in the package README. It produces the nested prefix terms `A2 A1 x`, `A3 A2 y1`, and `A3 A2 A1 x` without a clean target, a dirty connector, or an inverse cleanup. More generally, n stages call each `A_i` once, while independent source-path expansion calls it i times.

The complete local bill separates map calls, scalar staging, root program/control, row hosting and handoff adapters. For n=3 the map-call comparison is `c1+c2+c3` versus `c1+2c2+3c3`. The target-hidden expansion also needs three clean scratch rows, three copied target rows, `9L` scalar staging writes/XORs, and six additional full rows; the chain needs no additional row or scalar staging. The L=2 noncommuting U/L/U fixture uses 6 map XORs in the chain versus 12 map XORs plus 18 staging operations in the expansion. Program and allocation costs remain separate charges.

## Provenance and related work

- Track `recursive-interfaces`; task `persistent-boundary`, changed scope; seed `68355377be950fd65aa0152ad8e7c722`; priority revision 3.

## Research: local-move exhaustion on the pivot-566+554 T74 supplier, and idle-optimality of the 249/417 dispatch (no new κ)

Since PR1800, κ ≈ b(supplier) up to the free slacks, so only a cheaper T74 supplier can raise it. This package gives exact, reproducible negative results for the cheap local move families on the current base and extra words, which are the same bytes as PR1839/PR1672. It also gives an ILP certificate that the owner packing's idle side is already optimal.

**Results** (`research/t74-k554-local-exhaustion/RESULTS.json`; raw data in `data/`)

- **Deletion relaxation of all 1,797 B reads** (exact frames). 1,002 deletions would lower cost.
  - Exactly 16 save one rank-2 split (−4,913 units): the early pivot reads of 448/450/452/454/585/587/589/591/473/497/521/545/586/588, plus the two costly reads inside the 566/554 kernels (B1, B3).
  - The rest are delivery reads, first writes and structural reads, from −3,050 to −26,389.
  - All 1,002 send value into target rows, so compensation must stay inside B. None can be moved to the frame-free cleanup prepends.
- **Frame-cost oracle**, calibrated exactly on PR1672's pivot-554 kernel. Its insert costs are `[0, 4913, 0, 0]`, so the kernel's whole cost is one rank-2 split. The cost-aware search rediscovers a −1,850 kernel by itself.
- **107 cost-aware compensation searches:** no negative delta. Every one-split read needs at least one split to compensate. Large-gain reads have single-window source values or rows that no candidate can reach.
- **Exact single-gate commuting-move sweep:** all 1,002 gain-carrying reads at all 4,461 window positions, exact solver. Results: 2,131 neutral, 2,330 infeasible, **0 gains**.
- **A section:**
  - A1220/1226/1232/1238/1244 are cold-pivot pre-cancels, each saving 6,763 if deleted. Compensating them across A, B and tails, with full-program exactness and the dirt rule, is infeasible.
  - 91 rewrites of a cancelling read pair into reads of the pivot's writer are all frame-infeasible.
- **Owner packing (aggregate ILP over all T74 child windows):**
  - Moving any K = 12, 24, … extra calls to base is infeasible.
  - Over every mix of the 0–4 entrance-demotion variants (W_res 3734–3738), the maximum number of empty rank-48 children is **22,748**. That is the current value, attained by 249 base / 417 extra.
  - So no supplier-mix or modulo-48 rebalancing can add idle rank-48 children.

**Reproduce:** `python3 -B research/t74-k554-local-exhaustion/verify.py --work /abs/new/work`. It takes about 5 minutes on 2 cores and checks:
- pins and profiles;
- the oracle calibration;
- 32+32 sampled exact re-solves;
- the 16 one-split searches;
- the packing ILPs;
- result consistency.

`--full` re-solves everything and takes several CPU hours. The receipt is in `evidence/`.

**Scope:** finite searches of the stated move families on two fixed words. This does not rule out multi-gate rewrites outside these families, new kernel mechanisms, or parent/centre-interface changes such as centre-path sharing (PR1708/1748/1791). No κ is claimed and no construction is changed.

Four whole-helper placements improve the currently selected PR1094 T16 packing from conditional **κ = 0.001672660197076918** to **0.001672664045494084** (+0.000230077643548%). The local R480 supplier, widths, 144-call order, physical stock and bit supplier are unchanged.

A two-move vacancy path exposes an eight-slot suffix; two width-four helpers from distinct calls fill it. The complete profile changes by `H7 - 2 H3 - H1 < 0` for every `Hr = r^p`, `0 < p < 1`. Only four of 69,120 owner rows change. `MOVES.json` gives every before/after row, and `build.py` reconstructs the data and bindings without an optimizer.

Validation:

- The unchanged strict T16 verifier passes all 11 stages, including fresh controller emission, audit and finite invoice; 69 admission, 12 bit, 15 controller and six independent owner rejection controls pass.
- Both exact moment engines and 47 strict outer inequalities per native/conservative assembly pass. The complete published wrapper also passes locally on CPython 3.14.8; registered Python 3.12 CI is declared.
- All 278 external inputs are pinned and declared for CI invalidation. Frozen predecessors are unchanged. Native local ancestry is source-bound reuse, not a new cold rebuild. Package metadata and diff checks pass.

This is an improvement to the **selected PR1094 benchmark**, not the best known packing of that supplier. [PR1407](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1407) already reports **κ = 0.001672680818492982** for the same unchanged supplier; this PR provides a compact four-row alternative. The two patches overlap at owner rows2010 and34306 and affected bins, so they cannot be composed as written. PR1154, PR1992 and PR2044 also report higher values for changed suppliers or transfer assumptions. All inherited all-size/compiler, realization, hosting, precision/tape, recovery, analytic and bit H1-H5 assumptions remain; no unconditional theorem or global packing optimum is claimed. The selected certificate is not edited.

[philippeVV's independent review](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2077#issuecomment-6176996271), with disclosed Claude assistance, reports full CPython3.12 strict/registered replay and metadata-check passes, plus a separate seed67 owner audit with eleven rejection controls and no blocking finding. The package now explicitly states that offsets reserve static disjoint prefix slices; their order need not match the unchanged call chronology.

Reproduce from a complete checkout:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-t16-vacancy-chain/verify.py --work /absolute/fresh/output
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-t16-vacancy-chain --check-only
```

The 54 real-file cases produce 28 invoice rejections and 26 survivors; actual assembly rejects another 16. The ten remaining cases are classified explicitly: four changed templates are rejected by the original upstream controller, two control-run flags by the isolated original final-binding assertion, two are unread controller metadata, and two are conservative retained allowances whose changed bytes violate the selected upstream pin. This is not a complete-chain acceptance bug or a new bound.

The useful finite boundary evidence is input-driven: a 511-bit prefix passes invoice while 512/513 are rejected; row 20159 passes while 20161 fails; adjacent logical allowances straddle the exact gate; and a mass-preserving rank-52 mutation fails halving. A quantified argument, with exact integer bound checks, explains why five other finite guards follow under explicit positivity, row and logical hypotheses. The four controller-rejected template survivors also show why the numerical invoice alone is insufficient to admit arbitrary bridge or owner semantics.

All changes are in `research/t16-invoice-boundary-audit/`. The source/fixture archives, selected overlays, retained input and arithmetic engines are pinned. No frozen stage or selected record changes. Each mutant rebinds hashes to actual bytes, crosses the production JSON boundary, and restores the honest fixture. Positive invoice and assembly reproduce the archived evidence before any negative outcome is interpreted. `EXPECTED.json` records exact rejecting statements and finite quantities; `VERIFY.json` registers a bounded stdlib replay.

prs.body:
## Result and scope

**Completed, author-checked verification engineering. No new supplier, paid profile or κ.** This adds an opt-in, source-authenticated caller that actually executes the unchanged selected PR1094 final supplier stage and compares **all 105 strict outputs plus its complete 13-line outer log** against the reviewed archive.

It completes the explicit caller-composition handoff from [PR2040](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2040) and [PR2059](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2059), rather than repeating their comparator or invoice-subgraph audits. Both small predecessor predicates are reused byte-for-byte with immutable source pins and attribution. Only `research/selected-final-replay-closure/` is added: 11 files, no frozen caller/source archive/shared index/selected pointer edits.

PR1824's original caller requires exactly 102 byte matches, one relocation and two timing differences, then raw assembly equality. PR2040 reports a Linux supplier replay that passed but violated that comparison because invoice object order changed the invoice's raw hash and both consumer references. PR2059 provides only the three-node authenticate-before-rebind predicate. The new caller composes that predicate with complete output coverage, actual stage execution, exact input roles and coupled execution receipts. PR2040's Linux observation is credited, **not presented as a Linux run here**.

## Complete comparison boundary

`POLICY.json` closes the boundary at 94 JSON/gzip-JSON outputs and 11 inner logs. Both sides must have exactly the full inventory, including when byte-identical.

Before comparison, each side independently authenticates **30 raw reference edges**:

- **2 invoice edges:** both `input_sha256/fresh_invoice` links must hash the actual same-side invoice. Only those two digests are then rebound. The complete canonical invoice and both complete consumers are compared.
- **22 log edges:** both receipts contain the same eleven ordered, successful stages; their complete arrays agree within the run, including time. Every log reference hashes that run's actual log, and all eleven logs are compared byte for byte across runs.
- **6 input roles:** the independent receipt must name exactly three work inputs, two local inputs and the source owner input, with their actual hashes. Only these six exact keys become fixed role keys. No other strings/keys undergo root-prefix rewriting, and receipt paths are never followed to read files.

Only **22 fresh stage timing fields** may vary across runs. They must be present, finite, nonnegative numbers, not Booleans or strings. All **12 copied historical timing fields** remain exact. The complete outer log checks eleven ordered stage lines against the same-side times and two exact final-result lines; no blanket line/token stripping occurs.

Every other field and digest stays in the complete strict typed comparison. Duplicate keys and nonfinite JSON reject; exact Decimal comparison avoids binary64 rounding; Boolean/integer distinctions and unknown fields are retained. Generated gzip containers are compared by decompressed payload rather than compression headers. Diagnostic classification counts are not acceptance conditions.

**Critical implication:** authenticating raw links alone does not establish semantic equality. The entire invoice is compared, so changing it and repairing both links still rejects. Likewise, changing an inner log and repairing both stage references still rejects. The finite controls exercise both cases.

An exploratory census found 173 hash-valued leaves matching output bytes, including semantic hashes and multiple byte-identical candidate targets. The caller does **not** infer roles from hash coincidence, normalize those other digests, or claim arbitrary reserialized-DAG admission. This is the complete declared invoice-format/root-role/fresh-timing caller boundary, not universal portability or a production mathematical false-acceptance claim.

## Sources, task and novelty boundary

- Scientific base: `564148b82ae9df72163f22106f15e73efca8aff2`, priority revision **4**. Selected κ remains `836330098538459/500000000000000000`.
- Contribution commit: `a247ef876e50bf3a7d890c7c1f9b409576674d7d`.
- One-shot chooser seed: `a1c9b8df7348849ae3ec156120abe878`; track verifier-engineering, card `portable-replay`. Complete output is `SELECTION.json`; concrete TASK was written before substantive computation.
- Scope refinement: complete the named full-caller handoff, not another root calculation, source invoice micro-audit or metadata-only check. Revision4 relevance is a trustworthy evidence boundary for the binding selected supplier.
- [PR1824](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1824): `ad5b1248f25a71983b20617e2f3a80be22f03990`, source-bound final-stage replay and original comparator.
- [PR2040](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2040): `d31c1418c0c23994d1444dbd9d356b9a8238fd5e`, strict typed comparison and reported Linux invoice-format observation.
- [PR2059](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2059): `323703a83640f4c104469bf29db18d7d579cb587`, authenticated three-node invoice predicate, explicitly not a full caller.

All **42 live repository inputs** are raw-SHA256/Git-blob pinned and declared for replay invalidation, including the selected stage package, strict upstream inputs, complete copied frozen base, archives and receipts. Both vendored predicates are authenticated before import. The ten local inputs are recovered from PR1042's archive and checked against its complete receipt. The reference output is additionally bound to committed PR1094 assembly/execution receipts. The reviewed archive omits `source/`, so its owner reference is checked against the separately pinned selected package input, not a fabricated archive member.

Submission checkpoint main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` changed guidance only; catalogue, scientific sources and selected record were unchanged. Revised guidance was read and the scientific base retained. Shared complete overlap snapshots covered 353 open PRs including drafts at 19:00:33Z and 738 discussion/comment/reply records at 19:02:09Z on 2026-10-14. Targeted local/cached queries and live PR2040/2059 heads were checked at 19:04Z; heads were unchanged. Search absence is not claimed as novelty.

## Actual validation

CPython **3.12.12**, macOS **27.0.1 arm64**, standard library. Direct final scientific smoke: **268.58 s**. Metadata/source pins plus registered replay: **261.47 s**. Both scientific executions freshly ran the unchanged supplier stage. The registered parent uses `-I -O -B`; the supplier child runs without optimization and with inherited `PYTHONOPTIMIZE` removed, retaining its assertions.

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -I -B research/selected-final-replay-closure/verify.py
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-final-replay-closure --check-only
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-final-replay-closure
```

Observed:

```text
PASS_FRESH_SELECTED_FINAL_STAGE {"bytes": 103, "json-diff:declared-timing": 2}
PASS_SELECTED_FINAL_REPLAY_CLOSURE files=105 edges=30 positives=5 negatives=287 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/selected-final-replay-closure outcome=completed
```

The deterministic `RESULT.json` records **5 constructed positives and 287 negatives**, separately from fresh supplier execution:
- every one of 105 file omissions, one extra output, and one semantic mutation in every one of 105 outputs reject;
- changed invoice/log contents reject even with both corresponding references repaired;
- valid invoice formatting composed with six role relocations and all22 stage-time changes accepts, as do a coupled outer log and a generated gzip-container change;
- stale links, role aliases, timing omissions/invalid types, all12 changed historical times, duplicate keys, Boolean/integer substitution, truncated gzip, outer-log faults and an immutable archive-header mutation reject.

This is a bounded per-output mutation census, not an exhaustive per-node census or a formal implementation proof. No hosted CI pass is asserted.

## Limits and next useful question

This is **not** `make frontier1094-verify`: ancestors are not rebuilt; their local scalar/native/phase evidence is reused from authenticated archives. The unchanged final stage does run restore/bind/lift/emit/audit/invoice/assembly/admission/bit-control/independent-T16 checks. No Linux/Windows execution, full cold ancestry, formal kernel, new κ, or inherited all-size/compiler/common-label/hosting/precision/tape/analytic discharge is claimed.

Next useful task: select one earlier PR1042 stage and derive an equally complete source-bound output/reference policy. Success requires actual stage replay plus complete field and semantic-fault coverage; stop rather than normalize unclassified digests. This needs separate overlap review and that stage's native dependencies. The present full final-stage replay takes about 4.5 minutes on the exercised host.

## Attribution and assistance

Credit Josie Elliston (PR1824); commdata2338 (PR2040); Adam Gall (PR2059); Maxime Fleury and Antoine Olivier (payload/container convention); and Rohan Arun, Jeremy Kothe, Hao Yan, Douglas Colkitt and the retained selected supplier/compiler lineage. Both comparator files and predecessor notices are preserved unchanged.

Prepared for @adamgall with **substantial OpenAI Codex assistance** in design, implementation, experiments, tests and writing. New work Apache-2.0. No independent human review is claimed.

## Three-total root-unit decoders: reductions, a sharp example and the remaining lift question (no κ claim)

Package `research/three-total-decoders`. Builds on the merged #1590 (Lemma A for T ≤ 2, lift identity Lemma B, ERR1, D5 CNF); the DRAT certificate of the D5 CNF is the pending #2031 and is not duplicated.

**Claimed** (each labelled PROVEN / CHECKED / OPEN in the README, with its script):
- **Reductions (PROVEN):** Lemma SCC (strong components), Lemma Peel (unit-support points/lines), monotonicity, and the structure of a minimal counterexample to (A) (cost = v − 1, every one-line deletion tight, no rank-critical line).
- **Partial theorems (PROVEN):** M1 (cost ≥ v/2 if no point has full support, any field), U (unit world: certificate ≥ |G| + |I|/2), the F2S identity cost = 3ρ − Σw_j ≥ 2ρ.
- **Sharp example tied_min (PROVEN, computer-assisted in one step; CHECKED):** 12 lines, cost exactly v = 12 by an exchange proof; all 217 optima enumerated, all lift to Q.
- **Certificate limits (CHECKED, solver results recorded):** order/label/multi-copy/2-adic certificates stop at 11 on tied_min; on the 19-line cex_min_1 the one-copy certificate stops at 18 while the stored multi-copy certificate (verified here) gives 20 ≥ v.
- **Lift route (PROVEN + CHECKED):** Lemma W′, Theorem 9.3 (joint signability is one F2 linear system; checked against an exhaustive oracle on 53 instances), the Čech-only obstruction, counterexamples (whole-matrix TU fails at v = 9; non-regular minimisers; K22-free does not give TU-signability; peeling induction PP is false).
- **X1 (G1-joint):** the statement "some cost-minimiser admits one signing with all three blocks TU" is **false** (exact counterexample v = 7: 4 minimisers, block 2 not TU-signable in all four, odd-theta obstruction; 14 instances in all, (A) holds on each). Hierarchy: whole-B TU (false, v = 9) ⇒ joint block-TU (false) ⇒ G1′ (same-support rank-preserving rational lift, OPEN) ⇒ (Q ≤ F2) ⇒ (A) via Lemma B. An exact minor computation gives an explicit same-support lift for every minimiser tested: all 4 of the v = 7 example, the first ≤ 12 minimisers of each of the 14 instances, 8 sampled gadget minimisers (102 lifts, re-checked exactly in `verify.sh`). The open core is (Q ≤ F2) (min Q-cost over rational B′ on incidences plus diagonal ≤ min F2 cost); same-support lifting is a convenient witness and probably not the final form (degenerate [[I,F],[G,I]] family, recorded).
- **X2 (Hesse over Q(ω)):** NONE FOUND. 1600 random Hesse-derived configurations (exhaustive over all B) and 90 hill-climb restarts: min cost − v = 0, none below v. So (A) also holds on all tested Hesse geometry; the lack of a field order is not supported as the mechanism. Evidence only.

**Not claimed.** No κ gain. (A) (cost ≥ v at T = 3) is neither proved nor refuted; no window is closed here; the 2²⁹ gadget enumeration, the CP-SAT certificate solves and the Hesse experiment itself are recorded, not re-run.

**Verify.** `bash research/three-total-decoders/verify.sh /fresh/dir` (python-sat and `cc`; single process, about a minute; step 0 checks `MANIFEST.sha256` and `SOURCES.json` and stops hard on mismatch; the five C programs are compiled from source; 36 PASS lines including step 0).

## Where characteristic 2 starts to pay: a T² threshold for root-unit decoders (E6 ties, E7 first gain found; no κ claim)

Package `research/char2-threshold`. Model, cost formula and lemmas are those of the merged #1590 (exact decoders, Lemma B, ERR1) and of #2111 (three-total decoders); this PR adds the explanation of *where* an F2 gain over v first appears.

**The law (argued).** For root units the dense F2 cost of the full orthogonal pattern is about T × (block rank), the block rank is about T, so a gain over v needs more than about T² lines.

**Table (CHECKED, exact; cost of an admissible pairing for the exact decoder M = Gram):** D4/D5/D6 tie (cost = v = 12/20/30); E6 ties exactly at 36 = 6² (stored basis and B; B0 costs 37 in the first-independent basis); A4–A6 above v (B0 upper bounds 16/25/36; annealing found 16/21/34); **E7 is the first gain found (49 < 63, T = 7; also checked in #1590, G3.E7-dyadic)**; E8 (72 < 120) is known (#1590 ERR1). The E6 B0 value 37 is checked in #1590 (G4.E6). F4 ties at 24 (recorded).

**Fano Levi graph (CHECKED, exact):** it realises over Q at T = 4; the exact minimum F2 cost of the stored realisations (rank(PQᵀ) = T, all T blocks nonempty) is 9 (T = 4) and 13 (T = 5) against v = 7: no gain at that size.

**Realisability (RECORDED, numerical):** the Sp4 doily (15 points) realises at T = 4 and not at T = 3; the 63-point Sp6 realises at T = 7, and Levenberg–Marquardt found no realisation at T = 6 or 5. No exact rational realisation is shipped, so these are not CHECKED.

**Scope.** The searches (annealing, cliques, lattice pools) are not exhaustive and are recorded, not re-run; the table costs are costs of specific B (upper bounds on the F2 minimum). There is no claim that T ≤ 6 can never beat v; the law is an explanation plus evidence. No κ claim, no window closed. Context: #606, #1698, #1830.

**Verify.** `bash research/char2-threshold/verify.sh /fresh/dir` (Python standard library and `cc`; seconds; step 0 checks `MANIFEST.sha256` and `SOURCES.json` and stops hard on mismatch; 10 PASS lines including step 0).

## Result

This package gives a scoped exact census for six read-only sources using thirteen singleton calls and one atomic `TRIO_{j,k,l}` connector call. Across all canonical 13-step words whose 16 total source-map applications restore every source at even multiplicity at least two, the maximum number of nonzero masks obtainable with paired readouts is 61/63. The search covers both possible source-map profiles, `(2,2,2,2,4,4)` and `(2,2,2,2,2,6)`, and allows repeated prefix states.

A maximum path repairs its two missing masks with four readouts each. The completed bill is 14 source calls plus 130 output readouts, 144 root calls total. The incumbent uses 16 singleton source calls plus 126 output readouts, 142 total. The source-map profile is unchanged. For uniform source-call frame/dispatch price `f`, output-readout price `g`, and all incremental TRIO costs `rho`, the cost difference is `-2*f + 4*g + rho`; at unit prices the candidate costs `2 + rho` more. No kappa or supplier improvement is claimed.

## Exact evidence

- The Python census enumerates 9,321,312 complete six-label restricted-growth words; 2,342,340 match the restored source-map profiles. The full histogram and fixed-width record digest are in `CERTIFICATE.json`.
- An independent C++ implementation recomputes pairwise prefix XORs directly and agrees on the profile count, maximum (61), maximizers (88), and complete histogram.
- Positive control: the pinned incumbent 16-singleton word covers all 63 nonzero masks.
- Negative controls: an invalid multiplicity profile and an out-of-alphabet label are rejected.

Reproduce from the repository root:

Base commit: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`. Selected-record SHA-256: `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`. Pinned inputs and source blobs are listed in `SOURCES.json`.

## Research: split-key kernel search on the T74 pivot-566+554 base word (no new κ)

**Stacked on #1957.** This branch carries #1957's commit unchanged, with Rohan Arun's authorship, because the tools and words come from it. Review only the second commit: `research/t74-split-key-kernel-search/`.

### Why this question

In the open κ claims built on PR1673's capped outer (#1928 and predecessors), κ sits within 1e-10010 of the T74 complex supplier's own saving. So only a cheaper T74 local word can raise it. The last two real gains were single **helper-donor kernels**: #1625 at pivot 566 and #1672 at pivot 554.

- Each kernel deletes a read whose removal saves a rank-3 split (−6,763 units).
- It restores exactness with inserts that cost one rank-2 split (+4,913).
- Net: −1,850 units per call, about +4.1e-8 in κ.

#1957 found no third kernel. Two things limited its coverage:

- its compensation family only reads registers holding **a multiple of the deleted read's source value**;
- it priced only 327 of the 3,451 A-section gates.

### What this adds

1. **The rest of the A-section deletion relaxation.** It prices the other 3,124 gates; all 3,451 now solve exactly.
   - 32 cold-pivot pre-cancels at −6,763 (A1215–A1246); 27 are new, since #1957 searched 5.
   - 48 accumulation reads at −8,857 (A3403–A3450); 40 are new.
2. **A split-key compensation search.** `tools/skkernel.py` generalises #1957's `abkernel.py`.
   - Inserted reads may use any value held by, or added into, the deleted read's source or target register.
   - The identity `Σ λ_j col_j ⊗ key_j = d ⊗ v` splits into one column equation per basis vector of the keys' span.
   - Values and columns come from the deleted word. Interacting inserts are banned: an insert that writes `x` may not precede an insert that reads `x`.
   - Every solution is re-priced exactly with #1957's `abkernel.price`.

### Results (`RESULTS.json`)

- **108 strict searches** cover every kernel-sized deletion (gain −3,050 to −8,857) in A and B: 32+48 in A; 2+4+4+2+16 in B.
  - 104 are **proven infeasible** by CP-SAT.
  - 4 are shape-infeasible (the −6,100 B reads).
  - **0 exact profitable kernels.** The only exact solutions are delta-0 relocations of the deleted read.
- **Positive control.** On #1672's pivot-566-only word, deleting B342 **rediscovers k554-signed-001 exactly**: the same five inserts, delta −1,850. Flipping one coefficient makes the exact pricer reject it as inexact.
- **Diagnostic.** For B783 and B802, the per-insert cap was loosened to 3× budget with no summed budget. The only exact compensation within 12 inserts is re-inserting the deleted read. So for these two reads the obstruction is algebraic, not an oracle-pricing artifact.

### Scope and limitations

- **Base word only:** `gauge44-word-566`, 249 of the 666 calls. The extra word was not searched.
- **First-order model.** Interacting inserts are not covered. Without the ban, the model proposed zero-oracle-cost B783 compensations that were inexact only because of interaction.

## Characteristic-2 shadows of rank-3 decoders: the anti-Fano bound by first-order jets, with a Lean-checked core (no κ claim)

Package `research/char2-jets`. Model, cost formula and lemmas are those of the merged #1590 (exact decoders, Lemma A, Lemma B), of #2111 (three-total decoders, the sharp example `tied_min`) and of #2125 (where characteristic 2 starts to pay); the Lean project formalises the rank argument behind Lemma B and its characteristic-2 twin. This PR studies the incidence pattern of a configuration over a field of characteristic 2.

**PROVEN (proofs in the README).** Lemma CR2 (a characteristic-2 realisation of the incidence pattern gives cost ≥ v for every B) with its tropical / 2-adic corollary, and Lemma A (T ≤ 2) as a one-line corollary; Theorem B2 (the map φ with φ(−1) = 1: cost ≥ v − |H| − |F| + MAS(W[F]); no wild incidence and no harmonic line gives (A)); Lemma VCR2 (a valued realisation whose diagonal dominates every directed cycle gives cost ≥ v) and Corollary J (a B-independent linear-algebra jet test); **Theorem T′: `tied_min` (the anti-Fano configuration of #2111) has cost ≥ 12 for every admissible B, by a first-order jet around its Fano collapse, with no SAT call and no enumeration**; Lemma F (the first-order obstruction is a binary flow of even incidence count). The generic-rank / split bound is proved; its completeness (equivalence with (A)) rests on a standard matching min-max that is quoted, not proved, and checked on instances.

**Lean (checked).** `lean/DecoderDuality.lean` formalises the core lemma `hadamard_diag_rank_sum`, Lemma B and Lemma CR2; no `sorry`, axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only. It does not formalise B2, VCR2, Corollary J, T′ or Lemma F. `verify.sh` does not need Lean (`LEAN=1` runs the build if `lake` is present).

**CHECKED (exact, `verify.sh`).** T′: the explicit jet satisfies (J1) on all 72 incidences and (J2) on all 12 lines, and 518 stored matrices B (217 optima, the full B, 300 random) have rank 12; stored CR2 realisations of 21 configurations are verified (all realise over GF(2) except `cex_min_1` over GF(4), so cost(`cex_min_1`) ≥ 19 for every B); `tied_min` is not CR2 over GF(2), GF(4), GF(8), GF(16); the 44 minimal non-CR2 sub-configurations (32 of six lines, tight); Corollary J on all 4095 sub-configurations of `tied_min` and on 1500 random all-harmonic configurations; Lemma A and B2 spot checks. **Recorded, not re-run:** the SAT enumeration of the 217 optima, 1889 of 1892 random configurations passing the jet test, the 400 B2 configurations, 300 wild-cycle configurations (all CR2), the split min-max on 300 instances.

**Jet failures (CHECKED).** On three random configurations jf0, jf1, jf2 a harmonic line cannot be moved at first order, and the order-2 diagonal vanishes identically on the first-order tangent space, so jets of order 1 and 2 give no B-independent certificate there. (A) still holds on them: exact minimum cost 12 (jf1, v = 9) and 14 (jf2, v = 9); cost ≥ 16 for jf0 (v = 11; "cost ≤ 15" is UNSAT; the exact value is unknown).

**Not claimed / OPEN.** No κ gain, no word, no window closed. (A) at T = 3 is neither proved nor refuted. Open: the "2-adic shadow" conjecture (every configuration over Q has a characteristic-2 valued realisation whose diagonal dominates every directed cycle); whether the Lemma F flow obstructs at every order on jf0..2 (orders ≥ 3 untested); a theorem for wild cycles (three-term incidences), which φ breaks; the min-max behind the split bound.

**Verify.** `bash research/char2-jets/verify.sh /fresh/dir` (python3 with python-sat and numpy, and `cc`; about one minute; step 0 checks `MANIFEST.sha256` and stops hard on mismatch). Optional: `LEAN=1 bash research/char2-jets/verify.sh /fresh/dir`, or `cd research/char2-jets/lean && lake build` (Mathlib at the pinned revision).

**Scoped negative result, no new κ.** In the abelian bit model of #468, two invertible rational 3×3 data targets still need six rank-one calls with one or two *clean* auxiliary registers (zero on input, restored to zero). Six suffice. Merged #1882 settled *dirty* auxiliaries for any register count and explicitly excluded clean ones. Clean correctness is strictly weaker: only the data columns of the endpoint are constrained.

## What is new

- **Clean low-span lemma.** #468 §3 / #1882 Lemma 2 survive clean ancillas. The projected rank argument reads only the data columns of `P−I`, so the auxiliary columns may be arbitrary. At five calls, the relation lattice therefore has rank ≤ 1.
- **Exhaustive check with the #1882 engine.** The acceptance predicate is relaxed to data columns; nothing else changes.

| Run | Words | Clean terminals | Clean-only | Candidates |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `n=3`, five calls (one clean ancilla) | 17,210,368 | 4,051,444 | 4,014,687 | **0** |
| `n=4`, five calls (two clean ancillas) | 24,883,200,000 | 4,012,291,456 | 4,012,108,024 | **0** |

"Clean-only" counts terminals that fail #1882's dirty predicate. Almost every surviving terminal uses the relaxation, and none gives two rank-three targets.

## Controls

- **Regression:** dirty mode reproduces #1882's pinned `n=3, s=5` terminal digest byte for byte.
- **Positive:** one target in three calls gives 64 candidates. Six calls with one clean ancilla gives 310,528.
- **Failure:** the out-of-model rank-two idempotent `E₀₀+E₁₁` gives 134,082 false savings at five calls.
- **Physical realisation:** 300 clean and 300 clean-only `n=3` terminals, plus 300 clean-only `n=4` terminals, are rebuilt with exact rational frames having exactly the stated relation lattice. Each formal product satisfies the clean predicate, and the clean-only ones fail the dirty predicate.
- **Independent symbolic check:** agrees with the engine on all `n=2` words, all 614,656 `n=3, s=4` words (full mode), and 3,646 `n=3, s=5` words.
- **Clean-only identity:** an explicit two-call word that is correct only because the ancilla is zero is accepted, and its leaking variant is rejected.
- **Tamper controls:** a dropped terminal, an altered representative, a false flag and a wrong-arity record are all rejected.

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 -B research/bit-clean-ancilla-registers/verify.py          # ~1 min
python3 -B research/bit-clean-ancilla-registers/verify.py --full   # ~2.7 hours, adds n=4 and s=6
```

Expected: `PASS_CLEAN_ANCILLA_SIX_CALLS`. Terminal streams are hashed rather than stored, because the full runs emit tens of GB. `RESULT.json` is the recorded full replay (macOS arm64, Python 3.11.9, Apple clang). A separate standalone `n=4` run gave the same digest. `scripts/research_package.py --check-only` passes.

## Scope / not covered

- Covers one and two clean ancillas. **Any number of clean ancillas is open**, because #1882's written Lemma 1 reads auxiliary columns.
- Three data registers with a clean ancilla at eight calls is not attempted.
- #288 §1.3(b) already charges clean ancillas, so this closes a route; it does not remove a charge.
- No change to κ, the selected record, `upstream/` or frozen evidence. Not a Lean proof.

Task: `bit-new-register-model` (scope key `7084092dd726e7ba1f2f`), scope refined (auxiliary input convention), research base `e112d71c`, rebased onto current main `0fdd7d82` (quick replay re-passed before rebase; package-only diff). The helper's random draw was `adversarial-audit`. I switched cards because this question continues directly from my merged #1882, and the overlap check found no prior work on clean ancillas in this model; #1882 and #1822 explicitly exclude them. Claim: #2073. Overlap was checked at start and again before submission.

Credit: Ali Romman (#468: model and low-span lemma), eumemic (#288: model and ancilla pricing), huxint (#203). The engine and controls are adapted from #1882. Prepared by waynenilsen with substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic). No independent human review is claimed.

Feedback: the generated `VERIFY.json` caps commands at 600 s, so the ~2 h exhaustive run can only be registered as `--full` outside the launcher.

## Change and mathematical scope

**Scoped query-model proofs and constructions; no new κ.** Adds `research/bidirectional-connector/`, centered on two results:

- **All-word lower bounds with matching asymptotics.** For \(M=2^n-1\) outputs, the optimal one-root and two-root query tariffs approach \(4M\) and \(3M\), respectively, over F2 and characteristic zero when \(a=1\), \(b\sim\sqrt{2M}\), port prices agree, and transfer prices remain fixed and finite. The lower bounds include source-locality corrections and allow arbitrary source-call counts and transfer depth. Matching constructions establish a **25% limiting query-tariff reduction** under these assumptions.
- **Signed zero-sum triangle.** A characteristic-zero construction uses two arbitrary dirty roots, with every child call at physical z0. For three source blocks with \(q_i=2^{|P_i|}\), its complete operator/transfer invoice is:
  ```text
  B = sum(q_i)
  A = 2M + product(q_i - 1)
  T = sum(q_i) + 4
  ```
  At \(n=15\), \(b=285\), \(a=\tau=1\), its tariff is **122,785**, versus a proved lower bound of **138,778** for every one-root word: at least **11.52%** less in this model.

Sources remain immutable, outputs are unobserved until completion, maps may be singular and noncommuting, and incoming root values are arbitrary and restored. Signed inverse calls subtract map applications; they do not require inverse matrices.

Supporting material includes a 73-call exclusion, a minimum-read walk compiler, minimum-source bounds, and signed dirty-cache constructions. The compiler does **not** minimize transfers across all minimum-read decompositions. Cache constructions explicitly require additional dirty rows.

**Limits:** extra root reservation, routing, preparation, precision, tape/head access and other costs outside the fixed call tariffs remain unresolved. No qualifying recursive caller, physical supplier adoption, integer-multiplication runtime improvement or exponent improvement is established. RAM benchmarks exercise deliberately expensive B maps and cheap A maps; they are checks of that tariff regime.

## Task and overlap

- Original task: `connector-alphabet-change`.
- Scope status: **changed**, from a tiny alphabet-extension experiment to scalable query-model bounds and constructions.
- Scientific baseline: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`.
- Current-main/guidance checkpoint: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4.

The connection to the bottleneck is conditional: an actual caller must support the required map tariffs, offline targets and paid root operations before these query savings can affect a recursive budget.

Nearest overlaps:

- [#2065](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2065), head `2721b1e31d718a6e70266a99521f629ce2e1d259`, establishes the six-transfer five-source endpoint. That endpoint is credited supporting evidence here.

- Our [#2227](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2227) concerns a separate scalar compensation network; no combined saving is claimed.

The last complete overlap snapshot, **2026-10-14 23:53 UTC**, covered 445 open PRs, 896 discussion/comment/reply records and 1,538 local records. prs.body:
**Status: research note and scoped negative result (bit supplier). No new κ, no supplier change, and no selected-record edit.**

## Question

PR1084 (`research/bit-orthogonal-pair-decoders`, navinor) showed that a decoder term with orthogonal punctured reader and source lines costs 6 instead of 7. It reached P102 (cst 54) over all 120 lines, but left two open points:
- At nine stages, the inventory R = 439 exceeds the hosting wall 4v = 408.
- The shipped PR589 puncture admits only one such pair (P110).

This PR asks a narrower question. Inside the family that actually built the selected bit word (PR555's `gen_p3` on PR543's frozen L3 plan), how many cost-6 terms can a legal reader set reach? And what are the resulting units worth at the nine-stage template and at PR555's eleven-stage template, once hosting, idle children and the generator's real helper inventory are all priced?

## Result

1. **P102 is unreachable in this family; the maximum is j = 5 (P106).**
   - The frozen plan has 19 eligible pseudo-target lines. Of the C(18,9) = 48,620 subsets, 17,478 are admissible.
   - The root-dual count j is distributed `{0:4515, 1:7975, 2:3977, 3:929, 4:77, 5:5}`.
   - The shipped P has j = 1 (pair 66–87, i.e. PR1084's P110).
   - A second implementation, written before reading the first, agrees on all 127 compared fields.
2. **At R = 439, eleven stages would look favorable, but that premise is false.**
   - Eleven stages host every unit whole (11R ≤ 64v).
   - At R = 439 the j = 5 sets would gain +1.94% to +1.97% over the selected bit c.
   - Real `gen_p3` builds of 4,989 reader sets need R(P) = 446–472 helpers, against 439 for the shipped set. PR555's `choose.py` minimised exactly these extra carriers.
   - With their own R(P), all 82 j ≥ 4 sets price between **−2.78% and −0.21%**.
   - None of the 2,785 built j = 2/3 sets passes the nine-stage wall (min R 446 > 436 for j = 2; 448 > 432 for j = 3).
3. **The only hostable gain is the shipped P110 at nine stages, +0.70%.** That is below PR1084's recorded P104 line (+1.3294%) and below the same P104 gain re-based to the current selected complex b (+1.9829%, a stated transfer premise). The bit side does not bind today; its headroom is 3.46%.

Exact parts:
- the census;
- template parameters and walls;
- the certified idle optima and window max-flow;
- every c, as a certified lower bound from the pinned selected-record engine.

Positive controls reproduce, exactly:
- PR589 at nine stages and at eleven stages;
- PR555 at eleven stages;
- a byte-for-byte rebuild of PR555's word.

## Premises and open obligations

- No P(111−j) word with punctured duals is built, and `gen_p3` does not model dead non-reader lines.
- The asymmetric rank-6 COPY (PR620) is unrealised.
- Profiles are PR589-based proxies with an average-helper shift for R ≠ 439. The margin to the nearest threshold is at least 1.5 percentage points.
- The receiver search is bounded, not a proof of minimal R.
- j = 2/3 coverage is time-capped at 281/929 and 2,504/3,977 sets, with a two-receiver screen over all 4,906.
- Eleven-stage use would need a new assembly receipt.
- The census fixes the label-reader basis.

This is a finite result for the frozen plan, not an impossibility theorem for orthogonal-pair decoders. The README lists three open next questions: a jointly optimised plan, realising the shipped P110 word, and pricing the built-word profiles.

## Reproduce

From the repository root (Python 3.10+, standard library only, about 100 s):

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-orthogonal-pair-stage-screen/screen.py --check
```

Expected last line begins `PASS_BIT_ORTHOGONAL_PAIR_STAGE_SCREEN rows=44 enum11=82 ...` and ends `| own_R: L11 j>=4 82/82 hostable, >=P104 0/82, >=rebased 0/82, best -0.211302% at R=451 ... checks=57`. It runs `census.py --check`, `independent_census.py` and `price.py`, and requires each of their PASS lines.

The build receipt `CARRIERS.json.gz` is regenerated by `carriers.py`. That needs numpy (2.5.4, verified PyPI wheel) and took 1,142 s on 4 workers; the README gives the exact command.

Checks run locally:
- All four scripts pass on CPython 3.14.4.
- `scripts/research_package.py --check-only` gives `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`.
- The 65 `test_research_*.py` tests pass (2 skipped).
- The registered Python 3.12 replay was **not** run, because 3.12 is not installed here. The scripts parse under the 3.10 grammar.

## New mechanism

This package tests the reversible selected-state shear

```text
X_T <- X_T + X_A
Y_T <- Y_T - X_A
```

between the fixed QQ16 F0 and B1 calls. It preserves each selected `X_T+Y_T` sum and uses existing fields. The exact source-pinned group-algebra replay propagates all eight directions of the retained selected-input erasure witness through B1. Without the shear the T output has rank 0; with it the T output has rank 8. This contributes the complete 66-module Lean toolkit for proving physical multitape computations and their costs. It combines the earlier foundations and all subsequent extensions in one self-contained package under `research/multitape-proof-toolkit`. External proof dependencies are Lean/Mathlib; every additional proof module is bundled, with source attribution, so contributors do not need a personal Lean tree.

The contribution includes:

- Finite machine models with local writes, unit head movement, relative and absolute tape semantics, execution and halting proofs, exact time contracts, and asymptotic cost transport.
- Verified homogeneous and heterogeneous TM2 compilation, physical simulation overhead, stack encoding/decoding, output recovery, and fixed bottom-anchor theorems relating final heads to final stack lengths.
- Locality, dirty-frame replay, finite footprints, spectator preservation, terminal observations, sequential composition, finite control embeddings, scheduling, and charged handoffs.
- Physical stream, parking, marker-installation/removal and restoration routines; arbitrary finite tape-bank embeddings preserve costs, and generic callers allow children to use additional work tapes and return explicit changed workspace. Closed marked and unmarked controllers have exact costs `6|x| + 5|y| + 18` and `6|x| + 5|y| + 24` respectively.
- Fixed-width and canonical binary output interfaces, including a five-state serializer that converts a padded LSB stack to an MSB word at origin zero in exactly `3m + 4` physical steps, erases the source, restores the specified heads, and preserves spectator tapes.
- A fixed six-tape unsigned multiplier: for all `a,b < 2^n`, it halts with the exact padded `2n`-bit MSB product at origin zero within `280n² + 314n + 117 <= 400(n+1)²` physical transitions. This includes input loading, output serialization and handoff, with width zero proved.
- Reused and attributed Problem 1.8 RAM/TM encoding, microcode, arithmetic and polynomial-cost proofs, bundled under public module paths.
- Pinned dependencies, source manifests, provenance, complete declaration/axiom auditing, rejection controls, replay scripts and an optional formal CI recipe.

Validation: a fresh rebuild of the exact uploaded package passed on Lean 4.34.1 with Mathlib pinned at `d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`. The defining-module audit covers 5,028 declarations, including 2,582 theorem declarations and 484 private declarations. No package axioms are admitted; only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` are allowed. Finite operational controls and actual Lean negative fixtures also passed. Hosted CI and maintainer review remain separate checks.

This supplies reusable proved infrastructure for future multiplication algorithms and cost analyses; it does not change kappa. The quadratic example takes two stack-encoded operands, retains explicitly described residual arithmetic workspace, and does not yet provide the serialized-input, alphabet and full-cleanup bridges needed to use it directly as a generic caller child. No fast recursive multiplication or complete cleanup theorem is claimed.

## Result

This package adds a scoped exact bill for six-source hyperedge connector calls of arity four through six. Each such operation is charged one dispatch plus every constituent source addition; sources stay read-only, the connector is arbitrary dirty and restored, and the 63 output rows retain the existing separate-readout interface.

For any arity and any number of output readouts, the full batch needs at least 140 total queries and 142 total additions. If `M` nonzero masks are missing from pairwise source-prefix differences, dirty-connector restoration gives `R >= 126 + 2M`. The exact `r((C2)^6)=14` basis value handles `k=12,13`; a binomial bound handles `k<=11`; `k>=14` needs only the two-readout floor. Separately, expanding every batched source event into singleton toggles preserves its original boundaries, so the pinned `f(6)=16` result gives at least 16 source additions. The attributed PR #2128 DUO word attains `(140 queries,142 additions)`. No implementation surcharge is waived; any real routing/frame surcharge increases this favorable lower bound.

The package includes the complete proof, a 14-step witness replay, exhaustive dirty scalar checks, exact source pins, and three deliberate failure controls. It does not claim supplier admission or a new `κ`.

PR #2338's all-batch P112 argument uses a normal-class rank implication that had not been kernel-checked here. This contribution formalizes that implication, its rectangular fixed-space transfer and its complete count/price consequences, with the exact premises exposed.

For any field and finite term set, distinct endpoint classes and `K[i,j] != 0 -> beta[i] = alpha[j]` imply `2 dim ker(I-K) <= t`. For rectangular factors with `AC+DE=I_N`, the same hypotheses on `CA` give `2N <= 2n+t`; charging every term yields `64k+3t <= 7t+8n` when `N=8k`, plus the real-power analogue. The proof includes empty term sets. Explicit counterexamples show why equal classes, zero diagonal alone and a one-third replacement fail.

The source mathematics belongs to DreamingOfClouds' #2338, pinned at `82700676e1d42acf98dc1921cb6ef82551620008`; exact README/NOTICE copies and hashes are retained. #2342 supplies a narrower independent three-call argument and explicitly excludes auditing the broader all-batch proof. This PR does **not** verify the geometric/frame premises, run the source SAT/DRAT rigidity check, audit all of #2338 or admit a physical supplier. Selected certificates and kappa are unchanged.

Validation performed locally:

- Fresh Lean 4.33.0-rc1 / pinned Mathlib build: 26 actual axiom probes, only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`; three false proof attempts rejected after valid imports.
- Independent fraction and binary rank engines: 39,157 labelled compatible matrices in Q and F2, both orientation minors, nine rectangular fixture cases and an abstract sharp complete factorization.
- Registered Python 3.12 replay and nine fault-control groups passed.
- Full kernel replay under optimized Python 3.14 from a Git-free, read-only 20-file execution snapshot produced an identical kernel receipt; all nine control groups passed and the snapshot was unchanged. This caught and fixed inherited read-only permissions on the new build directory.
- Scoped workflow executes the actual Lean build; hosted CI success is not claimed by the local receipt.

Replay: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/lean-normal-class-rank`. That default checks sources/finite evidence and explicitly does not run Lean. README documents the separate full kernel command; VALIDATION.json records the executed checks and their limits.

One fresh random draw selected independent-verification, second suggestion `formal-interface-lemma`; TASK.json records the scope change and no reroll. Canonical main remained `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4. Final overlap covered 607 open PRs and 1,137 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings.

Coordination: #2380. Open next question: formally bind the actual P112 normal-class/frame evidence to the matrix compatibility premise.

Gareth Davidson (@bitplane), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, implementation, verification and writing; no subagents or independent human review. Wrapper/workflow/control structure adapts our #2341/#2295 harnesses, with attribution. New finite engines import no predecessor checker.

## Change and mathematical scope

Add a pointer under “Research notes and verification contributions” to [Dan Brown](https://github.com/jdb19937) and [Kenny Daniel](https://github.com/platypii)'s end-to-end Lean proof of integer multiplication below n log n on Mathlib's finite Turing machines.

The fixed finite Mathlib machine multiplies every pair of binary-encoded natural numbers in worst-case time `O(n (log n)^(1−κ))` with **κ = 2^-34**. The theorem includes the complete compact runtime, all-input correctness, and the actual machine-step bound. This is an asymptotic exponent bound, not a measured execution speedup.

Correctness and runtime are proved without remaining algorithmic or analytic assumptions. The theorem's transitive axiom dependencies remain exactly `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.

## Task and overlap

Documentation pointer to an external completed proof, based on upstream `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`. This does not establish the selected conditional saving κ = `0.001672660197076918` or change the selected construction.

## Validation

The proof is pinned at [4f40b5bc](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/tree/4f40b5bc74235274835fe6952b9b90ac414786b0): [statement and machine model](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/blob/4f40b5bc74235274835fe6952b9b90ac414786b0/IntegerMultBounds/MathlibTM2/Statement.lean), [explicit and existential theorems](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/blob/4f40b5bc74235274835fe6952b9b90ac414786b0/IntegerMultBounds/MathlibTM2/Theorem.lean), and [completed-proof axiom audit](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/blob/4f40b5bc74235274835fe6952b9b90ac414786b0/CompletedProofCheck.lean).

The pinned [PLAN.md](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/blob/4f40b5bc74235274835fe6952b9b90ac414786b0/PLAN.md) records that the complete compact theorem and its import-closure axiom audit passed at saving `2^-34`. The [CI run for this exact source](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/actions/runs/38806501790) was cancelled; no successful CI run is claimed for this pinned source.

Checked the README-only diff, whitespace, and agreement with the pinned theorem and audit entry point. No new Lean build or historical certificate replay was run for this documentation update.

## Credit

[Dan Brown](https://github.com/jdb19937) and [Kenny Daniel](https://github.com/platypii) are credited as the proof's coauthors. The external proof remains in its MIT-licensed repository; this PR contributes only the README pointer.

## Open next questions

Independent review of the linked theorem statement and machine/time model. The binding margin is §5 compact-layer cost. Continue the structural improvements toward the selected conditional saving κ = `0.001672660197076918` while retaining the unconditional end-to-end machine proof and the same standard axiom dependencies.

Repeated compilation dominates this native nine-stage checker fixture: the unchanged GCC build takes seconds while both complete native word checks take milliseconds. This opt-in experiment uses ccache object reuse, fresh linking and fresh native execution, reducing the measured local build-and-replay median from **2.753 s to 0.240 s (11.46×)**. A fresh cache fill takes **2.942 s**; this is a repeat-build benefit, not a whole selected-replay or first-use speedup.

The source engine is unchanged `research/e8-bit-carrier-skeleton/code/bit/checkers/columns_k.cpp`, pinned with its JSON header and upstream notice. The two exact RAW6 fixtures come from our #2373 at `b52f87f5355ad9f02ca4ac4395117655ac1b19c7` (the #1188 baseline and Sagar Thakrar's #2115 deferred-undo word). Every timed sample runs all 1,327 columns, nine stages, signed-prefix bills and 18 omitted-bridge controls per word. All native receipt fields compare, except elapsed time and the exact input path after binding it to the complete consumed payload hash. Reference and cached object hashes agree within each run.

Ccache preprocessor mode uses content-based compiler checks, no sloppiness/remote storage and a fresh toolchain-content profile. Source and transitive-header changes preserving both size and mtime cause misses and mathematical rejection. Compile-option and profile changes cause misses; restored inputs hit; a corrupt private cache entry is rebuilt. A wrong word still fails after a hit. The seven actual controls run through the compiler/cache/executable chain.

Validation performed:

- Three interleaved uncached/warm timing pairs and one separate fill, GCC 15.2 / Boost 1.90 / ccache 4.12.3.
- Full experiment: 13 builds, 24 native executions (21 positive, three deliberate mathematical rejections), including 384 omitted-bridge controls in successful executions.
- Registered Python 3.12 replay: independent bitset checks of every dirty column and exact prefix bills, plus nine package control groups.
- Full optimized Python 3.14 experiment and nine groups from a Git-free read-only 18-file execution snapshot: all normalized native results identical, snapshot unchanged; medians 2.761 s / 0.241 s.
- Metadata/pins pass. A scoped workflow executes the actual native benchmark; no hosted CI success is claimed.

`BENCHMARK.json` records individual measurements, cache counters, commands and execution hashes. The standard registered command intentionally performs Python/input checks only; README gives the separate full native command. No production entry point, frozen source, selected certificate or kappa changes. Complete PR2373 legality/exporter/5/9/11-stage integration and production end-to-end timing remain open.

One fresh random draw selected verifier-engineering / replay-runtime / source-bound reuse, refined to this one measured boundary without rerolling.
