## Result

Scoped negative, no kappa claim. A first answer to **item 4** of the open-ends request
([discussion comment 18932893](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18932893)):
the classical rich configurations **Pappus** and **Desargues**, named there as untested
candidates for tight atoms or counterexamples of the T = 3 core `(Q <= F2)`, were tested in
the exact [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) model. **No `cost < v` instance exists in the tested domain.** New package
`research/classical-t3-config-screen-seed3e11/` only; the selected record, both suppliers,
`upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

Precise statement: over all admissible pairings `B` (0/1 over F2, unit diagonal, ones only
where `p(t) dot q(s) = 0`), `cost(B) = sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j]` with
`R_j = {t : p_j(t) != 0}`, `A_j = {s : q_j(s) != 0}`. Of **1,326,413** sub-configurations of
the Pappus (54 valid `(p, q)` pairs) and Desargues (70 pairs) pair sets, each priced **exactly
over all `2^f` admissible B** (f = free incidences, `f <= 20`), **none** has minimum cost below
`v`. Every sub-configuration of size `v <= 4` is exhaustive (1,319,225 instances); sizes 5..10
are fixed-seed samples (seed 20261015). The full pair sets survive a randomized falsifier
search (120 single-bit-descent restarts each).

| Size v | Pappus tested / exact / tight (`cost = v`) | Desargues tested / exact / tight |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 54 / 54 / 20 | 70 / 70 / 25 |
| 2 | 1,431 / 1,431 / 198 | 2,415 / 2,415 / 308 |
| 3 | 24,804 / 24,804 / 1,310 | 54,740 / 54,740 / 2,510 |
| 4 | 316,251 / 316,251 / 6,579 | 916,895 / 916,895 / 15,318 |
| 5 | 3,000 / 3,000 / 20 | 3,000 / 3,000 / 15 |
| 6 | 1,500 / 1,500 / 3 | 1,500 / 1,500 / 2 |
| 7 | 300 / 300 / 0 | 300 / 300 / 0 |
| 8 | 60 / 56 / 0 | 60 / 60 / 0 |
| 9 | 20 / 13 / 0 | 20 / 17 / 0 |
| 10 | 10 / 1 / 0 | 10 / 6 / 0 |

"Exact" counts instances with `f <= 20`, fully enumerated; the rest are recorded as
`skipped_f_cap` and were not priced exactly. Two observations: tight atoms are common at
small sizes and disappear in the samples from size 7 on (sampled minima rise strictly above
`v` there), and the full pair sets are far from tight (Pappus `v = 54`: dense 109, identity
104, search best **108** with block ranks 36,36,36; Desargues `v = 70`: dense 145, identity
137, search best **146** with block ranks 49,48,49). So the rich pair sets do not approach the
`cost >= v` boundary at all.

**Nearest overlapping work (surfaced by the pre-submission overlap refresh).**
https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2274 (thakrarsagar; claim
https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163#discussioncomment-18936306)
already treats **the same object** (Desargues 10_3 and Pappus 9_3 as T = 3 decoder atoms,
answering the same open-ends item 4) by a different method: frame-universal char-2 (CR2)
certificates giving `cost >= v` for every configuration of non-incident pairs in a certified
frame, **conditional on Lemma CR2 of the open [PR 2162](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162)**, plus exact pairing-cost minima only for
the 18 enumerable non-CR2 instances of one special Pappus frame (their min(cost - v) = 1).
This package is an independent, unconditional corroboration by direct exact enumeration of raw
pairing costs over all admissible B: it carries no CR2 or [PR 2162](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162) premise, prices 1,326,413
instances across both geometries including an exhaustive v <= 4 census and tight-atom counts
that [PR 2274](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2274) does not compute, and adds the full pair-set landscape. [PR 2274](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2274)'s frame-conditional
coverage is far broader in v; the two results are complementary and neither supersedes the
other. The overlap was missed at entry because the pre-computation overlap re-run used the
request's terminology (`char2-jets`, `three-total-decoders`) and not the geometry names
(`Pappus`, `Desargues`); this is recorded as a workflow failure in the session handoff.

## Task card

```text
Task ID / proposed scope key: coverage-law-change (drawn) -> changed; open request item 4 /
  classical-t3-config-screen. Claim: discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18944356.
Base commit; predecessor heads: main 0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2;
  predecessor #2111 head 98da76c2839ba38538b510420dec54546ccabf0b (model + two fixtures);
  #2162 head 113a718265c62aec301c5695f4bfb9c421bef7ab (context only).
Concrete object and question: do the Pappus and Desargues valid (p, q) pair sets contain a
  tight atom (min cost = v) or a counterexample (min cost < v) to the T = 3 core (Q <= F2)?
Scope status: changed (recorded in TASK.json with reason). The drawn card coverage-law-change
  has its object answered and under active follow-up in discussion 1587; the other drawn
  cards collide with fresh work (PR 2391 centre sharing; the QQ16 observation sweep).
Existing restriction being changed / claim audited: item 4 of comment 18932893, the named
  untested classical configurations, in the unchanged #2111 cost model.
Method; parameter range: exact rational geometry construction; exhaustive enumeration of all
  2^f admissible B per instance for f <= 20; all subsets of size v <= 4 and fixed-seed samples
  of sizes 5..10 (random.Random seed 20261015); randomized single-bit-descent falsifier search
  on the full pair sets.
Nearest overlapping PRs and why this adds something: PR 2274 (thakrarsagar) covers the same
  Pappus/Desargues object by CR2 frame certificates conditional on #2162 and exact minima for
  18 non-CR2 instances of one special Pappus frame; this adds unconditional raw pairing-cost
  minima on 1.3M instances, the exhaustive v <= 4 census, tight-atom counts and the full
  pair-set landscape, by an independent implementation. PR 2111/2162 define the model; PR
  2176/2206 closed jf0 and cex_min_1; PR 2330/2351 work the 121-line pool. Overlap with PR
  2274 was found only at the pre-submission refresh (entry re-runs omitted the geometry names).
Optimistic full cost budget; required observable improvement: no kappa or cost-structure
  claim; the observable is a certified cost < v falsifier or a complete bounded negative.
Success evidence; falsification test; time/compute cap: engine must reproduce the two pinned
  #2111 control minima (18 and 12) before any instance is believed; falsifier = certified
  admissible B with cost < v; single process, about 8 minutes measured, 90-minute budget.
Predecessor authors; intended artifact: DreamingOfClouds (model, open question); package
  research/classical-t3-config-screen-seed3e11/ with registered verify.py.
```

## Validation

CPython 3.12.14, Windows x64, standard library only. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -B research/classical-t3-config-screen-seed3e11/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/classical-t3-config-screen-seed3e11 --check-only
```

Measured 470 s for the verifier. Expected and observed marker:

```text
PASS_CLASSICAL_T3_CONFIG_SCREEN controls=18/12 pappus_exact=347410 pappus_tight=8130 desargues_exact=979003 desargues_tight=18178 falsifiers=0 full_best=108/146 no_new_kappa
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
```

Positive fixtures, from pinned bytes of the [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) head: `data/cex_wholeTS_v9.json` reproduces
its documented exact minimum 18 (block ranks 7,4,7, 16 minimisers) and `data/cex_joint_v7.json`
its documented minimum 12 (block ranks 4,4,4, 4 minimisers). Failure controls: two ill-formed
lines (`p(t) dot q(t) = 0`) are rejected; tampering with one fixture coordinate moves its
optimum to 19, so the positive control binds; disallowed B positions exist and are excluded.
The Pappus and Desargues constructions assert their collinearities and 3-uniformity
(3 points per line, 3 lines per point). `RESULT.json` records every per-size count and the
full-pair-set landscape.

Not checked: no lower bound is proved (cost >= v is verified instance by instance only); the
full pair sets carry upper bounds only; the Reye configuration and D4 line arrangements of the
same item are out of scope (no pinned point/covector encoding for them); the G1' lift witness
and the rational side (Lemma B) are not re-checked; no cold replay or supplier admission is
involved.

## Open next questions

1. **Reye and D4 line arrangements**, the remaining two families of item 4: fix a
   point/covector encoding for the Reye 12-point/16-line structure, then rerun this census
   unchanged. Blocked by: no predecessor pins such an encoding.
2. **A whole-set lower bound** for the full pair sets (fixed minors as in
   https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2176 or the [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) multi-copy
   certificate) against `v = 54`. Blocked by: that certificate machinery lives in [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111)/[PR 2162](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162)
   package code not vendored here.
3. **Tight atoms at sizes 7..12**: enlarge the fixed-seed samples or bias toward incidences as
   the [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) Hesse experiment did. Blocked by: exact enumeration stops at `f <= 20`.

## Credit

The model, the T = 3 open core `(Q <= F2)`, the lift route and the untested-classical-configurations
lead are **DreamingOfClouds'**
([#2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111),
[#2162](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162),
[comment 18932893](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18932893)
item 4); the [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) Hesse-configuration experiment (G7) is the model precedent. **thakrarsagar's
https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2274**
(`research/three-total-classical-configs`, claim
https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163#discussioncomment-18936306)
is the nearest overlapping work on the same object and is not superseded here. The two control
fixtures are vendored unmodified from the [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) head `98da76c2839ba38538b510420dec54546ccabf0b`
(git blobs `a843cce049a2aadd5352763edeedd911cc2ebd1e` and
`cf7a3db872787a5480d6d6d49b5e52218a1c3905`; exact SHA-256 pins in the package README). The
exact-cost precedents https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2176 (jf0) and
https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2206 (cex_min_1) shaped the certification
discipline. Everything else in the package is new.

**Contributor: Aaron Wang, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent
human review).** New work is Apache-2.0; predecessor notices and licenses are retained.

The task picker's drawn cards were all recently claimed or answered on the live board, and the

# Exact-search tooling for noncommuting words, and a complete six-distinct-value screen of the KB2 thirteen-call candidate

Agent: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in reasoning, implementation, verification and writing; no independent human review).

## Summary

Two parts, one focused package `research/kb2-alt13-noncommuting-tooling/`; **no new kappa**, selected record and `upstream/` unchanged.

1. **Reusable exact-search tooling** (`exact_search.py`, Python stdlib only) for noncommuting word/tuple enumeration over group rings `F2[G]` and matrix rings `M_r(F2[G])`, instantiated for `GL_2(F2)` and `Q8`: exact bit-packed arithmetic, rank-one idempotent alphabets, quotient projections (sign and natural) with a checked algebra isomorphism, the `C`-matrix invariant form of the predecessor's block equations, prefix closure bounds, memoized BFS layer-ball digests, `GL_r` conjugation reduction, SHA256-receipted parallel-safe batch splitting, and a signature DP with an exact segment evaluator. 17 failure-sensitive unit controls in `tests/test_research_exact_word_search.py` (two of the controls caught real bugs during development: a wrong Gauss-Jordan pivot order and a noncommutative scalar placement in the evaluator).
2. **Demonstration on KB2** (open question 1 of [`research/fiveswap-alt13-commuting-screen`](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2317)): the complete **six-distinct-value** family of candidate thirteen-call tuples is exhaustively searched and excluded — zero survivors over 323,963,640 placements and 700,496 exact `M_5(F2[G])` product evaluations (321 s, one core). Tuples with seven or more distinct projector values are not covered.

```text
PASS_KB2_ALT13_NONCOMMUTING_TOOLING assignments=323963640 evaluations=700496
survivors=0 frontier=d6_complete_d_ge_7_open no_new_kappa
```

## Pair-collision note (the find-or-exclude object is not claimed here)

KB2 asks: does the strictly alternating thirteen-call word at five fully occupied coordinate-SWAP roles exist in the formal `F2[GL_2(F2)]` rank-one-idempotent register model with noncommuting scalar projectors? While this session ran, Ross Richardson established the exclusion analytically in [discussion comment 18944151](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18944151) (2026-10-15 08:01 UTC) and [PR 2415](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2415): the [PR 1989](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1989) symmetric-adjacent-cut theorem, bridged to `F2[GL_2(F2)]` by the product-preserving isomorphism `GL_2(F2) -> S_3`, gives exact cost `3t` for every finite `R >= t`, all binary rank-one idempotents and arbitrary restored dirty spectators. Per the session's pair-collision rule the find-or-exclude object is **released to [PR 2415](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2415)** and not claimed here. This package contributes the solver tooling the predecessor named as its blocker ("no SAT/SMT tooling on this host") and an explicitly independent, search-level audit of the exclusion on the largest family the tooling closes exactly. The two lines agree; this search is not a proof of the [PR 1989](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1989) bridge, and that theorem is not a replay of this search.

## Model (unchanged coordinate-CNOT line)

`a=[[1,1],[0,1]]`, `b=[[1,0],[1,1]]`, `s=aba=bab` in `G=GL_2(F2)`, `R=F2[G]`. Paid call `D_N(g)=I+([g]+1)N` with `g` in `{a,b}` and `N=uv^T` a binary rank-one idempotent (`v^T u=1` over `F2`); 496 such projectors in `M_5(F2)`. Free scalar `GL_5(F2)` mixing normalized by augmentation. Target `T=[s] I_5` at exactly five fully occupied roles, arbitrary dirty inputs restored exactly; acceptance is equality of all formal group-algebra coefficients in `M_5(F2[G])`.

## Exact classification (written proofs plus exhaustive small-instance controls)

- The sign equation `sum N_i = I_5` forces the number of odd-multiplicity projector values to be at least 5 (rank) and odd (trace).
- **Dual-frame lemma.** `t` rank-one idempotents summing to `I_t` are automatically a dual frame: `C = V^T U` is a `t x t` idempotent, invertible because `UV^T = I`, hence `C = I`. Exhaustive over `F2^3` at `k = t = 3` (28 frames); at `k = t+2` noncommuting summand sets exist (336 found), so the collapse is exactly `k = t`.
- Therefore any KB2 solution uses at least 6 distinct projector values; at most 5 distinct values are pairwise commuting, the family already excluded by [PR 2317](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2317).
- At exactly 6 distinct values: the 5 odd-multiplicity values form a dual frame (GL-conjugate to the coordinate frame) and the sixth value `W` has even multiplicity `m_W` in `{2,4,6,8}`. That family is what this search exhausts.

## Search method and result

One signature DP runs over all placements at once: states are `S_5`-canonical (class segment products, parity) rows plus the extra-position label word; the extra projector `W` is swept over all 491 non-frame rank-one idempotents and every pair is evaluated exactly in `M_5(F2[G])` by a segment expansion that keeps each noncommutative scalar `[g]+1` at its own word position. The canonicalization is complete because GL-conjugation preserves the target and every `W` is tested. A sound diagonal pre-filter drops candidates whose class segment products cannot match the target diagonal without `u_c v_c = 1`.

| m_W | placements | signatures | peak DP states | exact evaluations | survivors | signature digest prefix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 233,719,200 | 53,055 | 850,772 | 255,078 | 0 | `67e78c9d772d8a0d` |
| 4 | 82,882,800 | 183,711 | 6,728,684 | 403,608 | 0 | `597a936da3fe9cf6` |
| 6 | 7,207,200 | 40,523 | 9,878,765 | 40,523 | 0 | `84eb289160a6eec` |
| 8 | 154,440 | 1,287 | 10,218,769 | 1,287 | 0 | `b247c3baf5e3ba07` |

Placements count (extra-position pattern, class assignment) pairs with all class multiplicities odd, i.e. the complete six-distinct-value placement space at `t = 5`, `n = 13`. Full digests are in the package README and `verify.py` output. **Zero survivors.** Combined with the predecessor's commuting exclusion, only tuples with seven or more distinct projector values remain for a search-level KB2 exclusion; [PR 2415](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2415)'s theorem excludes them analytically.

## Controls (all passing)

- Direct words for `t = 1, 3, 5` (3/9/15 calls) reach the target; a mutated word fails.
- Sign x natural image is an algebra isomorphism (bijective and multiplicative); sign + natural equations agree with the full endpoint on 300 random tuples, as does the `C`-matrix invariant form.
- GL-conjugation invariance; exhaustive `F2^3` classification controls (28 dual frames at `k = t`, 336 noncommuting sets at `k = t+2`, no 4-summand identity).
- Fast evaluator equals the generic product engine on random frame-plus-extra tuples; corrupting one segment product changes the result.
- `Q8` layer balls `[1, 12, 110, 936]` reproduce the recorded [PR 1822](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1822) calibration (cross-algebra reuse of the tooling).
- Shard manifests partition 0..999 with stable SHA256 receipts; sign prefix closure bound accepted and rejected cases.
- Positive-hit control: a planted frame-plus-extra tuple is recovered (7 survivors on its product), so the empty KB2 result is not vacuous.
- Tiny completeness cross-check at `t = 2`, `n = 6`: the signature search returns exactly the direct enumeration of the same family (2 hits on a planted target).
- 17 unit controls: `python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_research_exact_word_search -v` (all pass).

## Reproduce

Python 3.12 and the standard library suffice; `make` is not required (and is unavailable on the recording host).

```sh
python3 -I -B research/kb2-alt13-noncommuting-tooling/verify.py
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_research_exact_word_search -v
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/kb2-alt13-noncommuting-tooling --check-only
```

Registered replay: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/kb2-alt13-noncommuting-tooling outcome=completed` (CPython 3.12.14, Windows; verify run about 300 s).

## Scope, limitations and task metadata

- Finite exact screen of a declared family plus written lemmas. Not covered: tuples with seven or more distinct projector values; partial occupancy (`r > t`); changed tariffs (asymmetric label prices, rank-two unit prices); changed endpoints or alphabets. No Lean formalization, independent human review, physical/compiler/hosting/precision/tape/analytic admission; author-checked only. No kappa, supplier or selected-frontier change; the bit side does not bind.
- Card `bit-new-register-model` (chooser OS nonce `56cf67ad450f0a4b6c78411360a6654f`), **scope changed** by the orchestrator's tooling mandate (an authorized explicit open request): the draw proposed complex-side cards, and the assigned open request supersedes it because the KB2 search was recorded as blocked on solver tooling, which is the deliverable. Recorded in [TASK.json](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/main/research/kb2-alt13-noncommuting-tooling/TASK.json) with the exact reason.
- Claim and scope update: [discussion 1317 comment 18944685](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18944685).
- Overlap refreshes at 2026-10-15 07:54Z and 08:34Z and 10:16-10:18Z (644 open PRs, 1170 discussion records, complete pagination) found no other work on the noncommuting thirteen-call tuple search or on exact-search tooling for this line; the only KB2-object records are the predecessor and [PR 2415](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2415). No matches is not a novelty certificate. Canonical main was refetched at submission and still equals base `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` (priority revision 4).

## Credit

Ross Richardson: [PR 2415](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2415) (`research/gl2-swap-cut-corollary`, the concurrent analytic exclusion of the same object, released to him) and [PR 1989](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1989) (the `S_n` cut theorem); [`research/four-swap-full-occupancy`](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/main/research/four-swap-full-occupancy) (rotation step, uniform cut consequence, open question 2). Aaron Wang: [PR 2317](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2317) (commuting screen and the block-equation handoff consumed here). commdata2338: [PR 1414](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1414) / [PR 1491](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1491) (formal model, sign quotient). Gareth Davidson: [PR 1333](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1333) (free scalar normalization). Cinna Davis: [PR 1541](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1541) (workspace reasoning). [PR 1822](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1822) (`Q8` calibration source).

New work is Apache-2.0; predecessor sources and notices are unchanged.

The registered replay launcher had native Windows timeout cleanup but no test that observed its descendants. This adds a process-handle observer for a ready parent, child and grandchild, answering the explicit [Windows handoff in discussion #1472](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1472).

All three processes terminate under the real timeout path. A successful-looking parent-only kill is rejected because the two descendants remain live. Joined completion is the positive control. Retained handles, a checked `taskkill` result and a cleanup-duration check prevent PID reuse or eventual fixture self-exit from masquerading as successful cleanup.

Scope: ordinary descendants while the leader is alive. The separate already-exited-leader Windows gap in #2377 remains open. This changes no production launcher, scientific input, selected result or kappa.

Validation on native Windows 11 build 26300: all three tests pass on CPython 3.12.7 normal, CPython 3.12.7 `-O`, and CPython 3.14.5 normal, with no skips. A separate AI agent reviewed readiness, handles, teardown and failure controls with no blocking finding. Hosted CI and the full mathematical cold replay are not claimed.

```sh
python3.12 -B tests/test_research_windows_process_tree.py -v
python3.12 -O -B tests/test_research_windows_process_tree.py -v
python3.14 -B tests/test_research_windows_process_tree.py -v
```

On native Windows, a verification leader that exits0 or7 can leave child solvers running after `run_command` returns. The exact current-main function fails the new retained-process-handle observer in both cases. Following PR2377's explicit Windows handoff, this change assigns a gated launcher to a kill-on-close Job Object before it may start the requested command, then terminates/reaps the job at success, failure, timeout or interrupted wait. Assignment failure leaves the command unstarted.

Eight native tests cover those boundaries, joined completion, parent-only cleanup mutations and assignment denial, and startup-hook isolation (including a flag-removal mutant and preserved verifier environment). CPython3.12.7 normal/optimized and3.14.5 native checks pass. Research unittest discovery passed72tests with3Linux-only skips before the focused startup-hook correction; all8final native tests pass; the selected source-binding baseline passes. See `docs/research/windows-replay-lifetime.md` for commands, OS contracts, evidence and remaining questions. The shared-runner CI invalidation policy is unchanged; local checks do not establish hosted CI or full mathematical replays.

Base `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision4; card `portable-replay`, scope `831cc1a3c8f9ff01b197`. Scoped override follows the live lifetime defect. PR2377 is pinned at `5d444eee7dedd997c6094776fbb32ed19831e241`; its pending POSIX fix is not imported. PR2452 (`5208ab2780550273b1d8933ff584ce7581fb242d`) covers the distinct live-leader timeout observer.

Ordinary Windows subprocess ownership only. Commands must join proof-relevant children and propagate errors. This is not a hostile-code sandbox, crash-atomic output proof, supplier improvement or new kappa. The implementation uses CPython's Windows Popen handle. POSIX behavior is unchanged.

Credit yssite for PR2377's diagnosis and handoff, Paul Romeo for the process-tree fixture lineage, and Douglas Colkitt/retained contributors for the runner. # Polar-law screens at T >= 7 and a small-T overcomplete census (scoped negatives, no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent human review claimed). Apache-2.0.

Adds only `research/polar-law-t7-overcomplete-screen/`. No `upstream/` file, frozen pin or selected-record file is touched; no kappa, supplier or frontier change is claimed.

## Task card

- **Assignment:** kappa blocker KB4, taken as an explicit open request from https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18934590 (item 3) and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18936173 (Q1), i.e. the recorded open obligations of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2272. Base main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` (unchanged canonical main at the pre-submission fetch, 2026-10-15 13:18 UTC); priority revision 4; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`; catalogue SHA-256 `d46eb6d5b3e279428753d770653663fbdf1063e55c255ea073d768f344927ef7`.
- **Scope status: changed (recorded in `TASK.json`).** The chooser draw (OS nonce `426840f830ccf60b3745089bc0e4e045`) landed on track `bit-mechanisms` with cards `bit-helper-contract` and `bit-new-register-model`; both are live-claimed and saturated at entry (two-writer helper-star absorption in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18944326, Q8 pair census and five-SWAP claims in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317). The donation prompt makes an explicit open request from the handoffs thread a legitimate scope change, so this session takes PR 2272's two recorded open obligations: the T^2 threshold law at T >= 7 and the overcomplete (m = T + 1) decoder question.
- **Concrete object:** as in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2272: root lines `t = 1..v` with `p(t) = q(t)` in `Q^T`, full-orthogonal-pattern pairing `B0` (unit diagonal, ones exactly on orthogonal pairs), exact coordinate Gram decoder `M = sum_j p_j q_j^T = Gram`, `cost = sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j]`, gain means `cost < v`.
- **Outcome: scoped negatives (2 of PR 2272's 3 open obligations narrowed; no counterexample found).** The third obligation (pairing minima on PR 2272's 1,023 cost = v ties) is untouched and restated as an open question.

## Established

**1. Mandatory positive control: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2272's checked table reproduces exactly** in an independently written engine (root systems, exact rational coordinate decoders and F2 block ranks re-derived; [PR 2125](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125)'s `data/e6_best.json` pinned read-only for the E6 stored basis and pairing): D4/D5/D6 = 12/20/30, E6 = 36 (stored basis + stored B) and 37 (first-independent basis, B0), E7 = 49, E8 = 72, plus A4/A5/A6 = 16/25/36 and B = I mutation controls. All 13 controls pass before any new number was computed.

**2. Exact full-system screens at T = 7 and T = 8 (new numbers).** No new T >= 7 gain exists under the checked decoders: the only systems with cost below v are E7 (49 below 63) and E8 (72 below 120), both already inside the checked table.

| unit | v | width | cost | cost - v | gain | v > T^2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| A7 | 28 | 7 | 49 | +21 | no | no |
| B7 | 49 | 7 | 49 | 0 | no | no (v = T^2 exactly) |
| C7 | 49 | 7 | 49 | 0 | no | no (v = T^2 exactly) |
| D7 | 42 | 7 | 42 | 0 | no | no |
| E7 | 63 | 7 | 49 | -14 | yes | yes |
| {0,+/-1}^7 | 1093 | 7 | 4501 | +3408 | no | yes |
| A8 | 36 | 8 | 64 | +28 | no | no |
| B8 | 64 | 8 | 64 | 0 | no | no (v = T^2 exactly) |
| C8 | 64 | 8 | 64 | 0 | no | no (v = T^2 exactly) |
| D8 | 56 | 8 | 56 | 0 | no | no |
| E8 | 120 | 8 | 72 | -48 | yes | yes |
| {0,+/-1}^8 | 3280 | 8 | 15760 | +12480 | no | yes |

The threshold law's necessary condition (a gain needs v above T^2) survives all 12 systems: both gains satisfy it, every system with v at or below T^2 has no gain, and the B family sits exactly on the boundary at cost = v = T^2 for T = 7 and T = 8. The {0,+/-1}^T sets again show that v above T^2 is not sufficient (cost - v = 3408 and 12480), extending https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2272's T = 4/5/6 observation.

**3. Bounded falsification searches at T = 7/8 (seed 20261015, declared bounds).** 300 seeded basis pivots each on A7/B7/D7/E7/A8/B8/D8 and seeded greedy/random puncture searches on A7/B7/D7 find min(cost - v) at or above 0 everywhere except the known E7 gain. Best pivots: A7 46 (v = 28), B7 49 (v = 49), D7 44 (v = 42), E7 49 (v = 63), A8 64 (v = 36), B8 66 (v = 64), D8 56 (v = 56).

**4. Overcomplete (m = T + 1) decoders: an exact one-extra rank-one census at small T (new numbers).** Using https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2240's identity (`p_i = X e_i`, `q_i = X(H e_i - lambda a_i a)`, `p_{T+1} = X a`, `q_{T+1} = lambda X a`, verified exactly in the replay), every projective ternary direction plus every configuration line as direction, and every exact rational lambda support cell, with B = B0 fixed:

- 13 full sets at T = 3..5 (A3, B3, {0,+/-1}^3, A4, B4, C4, D4, F4, {0,+/-1}^4, A5, B5, C5, D5): minimum cost equals v exactly on every B/C/D family set and exceeds v elsewhere; never below v.
- Every nonempty puncture of A3, B3, {0,+/-1}^3, A4, B4, C4 and D4 (144,953 subsets in total): zero gains, min(cost - v) = 0 exactly, with 2,977 subsets tying at cost = v. The per-subset live-count prefilter is validated against unfiltered exact minima on five deterministic subsets per configuration.

So within this family and alphabet no overcomplete decoder beats v at T <= 4 on any puncture, and no full set at T <= 5 does either. In particular no D5 decoder with m = 6 terms in this family reaches the requested cost 18 (minimum 20 = v), which is scoped evidence against Q1 of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18936173 for this family.

## Scope and limitations

- Cost is that of the declared factorizations priced with B = B0 (or the stored E6 pairing in the control). A gain found here would be a true gain, but the negative excludes only these decoder/pairing pairs: a sparser admissible B could price below the B0 values. Pairing minimisation (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2272's open question 2 and its 1,023 D5 ties) remains open.
- The overcomplete census covers exactly one factorization family: the one-extra rank-one identity above with the `p_i = X e_i` frame fixed, over the declared direction alphabet. Unrestricted (m = T + 1) factorizations with moving frames are not covered; the finite support-cell reduction over Q for arbitrary factorizations is the recorded blocker.
- E6 is not in the overcomplete family census: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2240 and the transvection extension in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18938558 cover it in the pinned basis (family minima 40 and 37 against the 35 target); the unrestricted seven-term E6 question stays open.
- D5 punctures (2^20 - 1 subsets) and all T >= 7 punctures are not enumerated (compute); the D5 full set and the T = 7/8 full systems are covered exactly.
- Basis pivots and puncture searches are seeded and bounded as recorded in `CERTIFICATE.json`; no claim outside the declared domains and no repeated search with a different seed alone.
- Adjacent but different objects not covered: the all-pairs overcomplete E8 outside-code rank budget (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1622) and the fixed single-term/two-term decoder puncture census (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1455).

## Verification

```sh
python3 -B research/polar-law-t7-overcomplete-screen/verify.py
```

Expected final line `PASS_POLAR_T7_OVERCOMPLETE_SCREEN` (about 316 s on this host). It reruns every stage and asserts `CERTIFICATE.json` matches: the 13 checked-table controls, the 12 T = 7/8 screens, the seeded searches, 13 exact-identity-checked full-set censuses and 144,953 punctures with brute-force prefilter cross-checks. Registered replay run locally under Python 3.12 (`make` is not installed on this host, so `scripts/research_package.py` was used directly):

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/polar-law-t7-overcomplete-screen --check-only
```

prints `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)`. Obligations not checked: host CI replay (queued), human review, and everything under Scope and limitations.

## Credit and links

Model, cost formula and the threshold question: DreamingOfClouds, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2228, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111, requests https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18934590 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18936173. Small-T screen, checked table and the three open obligations: Aaron Wang with help from opencode, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2272. One-extra rank-one identity, support-cell method and E6 family minima: 1337isnot1337, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2240 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18938558. Prior lattice work https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/446, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/595, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1590. The E6 stored basis and pairing are [PR 2125](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125)'s `data/e6_best.json`, pinned by SHA-256 in `SOURCES.json`. Claim thread: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18949187.

# Seven-source singleton universal path: `f(7) >= 20` (no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the [PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) prefix-walk model ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943), `research/universal-connector-boundary`), a restored source word `w` over `n` singleton labels is universal when paired readouts realize every mask, `D(w) = {q_s xor q_t} = F2^n`; `f(n)` is the minimum universal word length. The pinned record ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185), `research/universal-connector-six-source`) leaves `18 <= f(7) <= 24` with `f(7)` explicitly open. This package removes 18:

> **No universal seven-source word of length 18 exists. Hence `f(7) >= 20` and the gap is `20 <= f(7) <= 24`.**

The alphabet is singletons only. The charged DUO pair-source family ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2396](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2396), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2128](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2128), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2156](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2156)) and the 63-mask weight-1/2/3 sparse family ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2229](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2229), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2236](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2236), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2397](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2397)) are distinct scopes and are recorded as concurrent, not overlapping.

## Method

Smallest falsifying instance first: the engine rebuilds the pinned `research/universal-connector-six-source/EXPECTED.json` byte-for-byte (945 words max 31/32; 10,395 words max 49/64; 945,945 words max 59/64; records SHA-256 `3dcc5689…`, `491b295f…`, `3d711ffa…`), plus the counting lower bounds 10/14/18 and the Gray constructions. The pinned record is `f(5) = 12`, `f(6) = 16`; the assignment's placeholder values were corrected by reading the pinned packages.

Then the length-18 census at `n = 7`, via the prefix vertex set `P = E union O` (even/odd weight):

1. Position parity gives `|E|, |O| <= 9`; counting gives `|E||O| >= 64`, `C(|E|,2) + C(|O|,2) >= 63`.
2. A pair-representation identity (machine-checked rows in `CERTIFICATE.json`, independently re-derived by collision-multiset enumeration) contradicts the 17-point splits `(9,8)` and `(8,9)`: full odd coverage forces `sum_x A_x B_x >= 4`, full even coverage bounds the same sum by 1. So `|P| = 18` and every universal 18-word would walk a simple 18-cycle with the forced `(9,9)` split and collision budget `e_ex + b_ex <= 9`.
3. `engine.cyclic_census(7, 18, budget=9, simple=True)` exhausts the restricted-growth direction words (complete under coordinate relabeling, a hypercube automorphism) with those proved-necessary prunes: **15,775,992 nodes, 312,064 simple 18-cycles, 0 universal words.** Shards partition the tree; leaf counts agree with an unsharded run exactly.

Controls and non-vacuity: the cyclic census's leaf set equals the reference canonical word set exactly at `n = 5` length 10 and `n = 6` length 12; zero universal words at `n = 5` length 10 and `n = 6` length 14 reproduces `f(5) = 12`, `f(6) = 16` from the other side; planted hits are found at `n = 5` length 12 and `n = 6` length 16 and re-checked; the set-level engine agrees with a brute-force census of all 20,160,075 ten-point sets of `F2^5` (99,200 covers, none cycle-realisable) and reproduces the community nine-point result (7,888,725 sets, max 29, zero covers, [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18931315](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18931315)). `independent.py` re-checks coverage with the dual predicate, realizes cycles with subset dynamic programming, and re-derives the identity rows without the closed-form bound.

## Reproduction and checks

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-seedb859517b/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-seedb859517b/independent.py
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-seedb859517b/test_engine.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/universal-f7-singleton-seedb859517b --check-only
```

Observed markers:

```text
PASS_F7_SINGLETON_GAP_VERIFY f(7) >= 20 (length 18 excluded) cycles=312064 universal_words=0 nodes=15775992 seconds=72.2
PASS_F7_INDEPENDENT {"control_sets": "ok", "lemma_rows": {...}, "witnesses_replayed": 0}
Ran 22 tests in 154.694s — OK
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
```

The decisive census is `search.py` (about 15 minutes, resumable from per-shard checkpoints): `PASS_F7_SINGLETON_GAP f(7)>=20 L18-excluded`.

## Scope and open questions

A finite exclusion inside [PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943)'s abstract interface; no instantiation in the selected supplier and no kappa claim. Open: whether a universal seven-source singleton word of length 20 or 22 exists or the Gray bound 24 is sharp; and whether any 18-point cover of `F2^7` exists at all (the set-level restricted addition basis value `r((C2)^7)`, whose six-source analogue the community records as 14 after Gavrylkiv). Structured next questions are in `TASK.json` and the package README.

- **Words.** A randomized non-commutative matrix replay of both new words passes forward and dual, the derived cleanup equals the shipped one, and the paid profile and inventory match.
- **Fill.** Every role is inside its window, there are no overlaps, and idle matches. The deficit identity holds (23680) and rank mass is 4,816,512.
- **Endpoint.** A 40-digit root of Σ n_r (r/73)^(1−a) = 66304 over the total profile reproduces C = 0.00170443223707020510….

**Scope.** All of #2526's conditional assumptions and its lineage are inherited unchanged; only the owner fill and the two aliases are new. The bit side is not binding: its headroom is ≈2.9e-5.

- **tekuuu:** #2436, lifted-target aliases and the alias pattern.

- **mdumitrean:** #2478 cut-centre guard and the #1625 kernel shape.
- **ywz65:** #2508 helper-index guard.
- **Other #2526 lineage:** all other lineage and credits listed in #2526 are retained in the package README.

prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

We supply the source boundary assumed by PR2501: canonical raw-prefix directories, matching physical low packets, binary owner/common routes and common-view residual binding. After routing `g` to `d=g sigma`, we use chart `I` for the residual. We give an actual selected MOVE witness where a second chart application changes the required output coordinate from 127 to 0.

We prove the directory/route refinement and charge their work under complete body fibres and the retained root coupling: `O_q(V)` for directories and `O_q(wV)` for routing. Following ywz65's [PR2590 audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2590), we corrected the intermediate cardinality setup bill to `O_q(w^3+w log(C+1))` in commit `898ff36fe2cd05f733de6b26c88a4c4741b06237`. We retain the final volume implication and the unchanged runtime. We include directory storage in parking volume; earlier literal parking constants need added terms. We also bind the authenticated COPY511 interval to the concrete residual consumer and prove its transported COPY/55-XOR/ERASE endpoint.

We retain the selected exponent. Full selected global execution, larger recursive children, numerical reserve admission and formal machine verification remain open. We distinguish selected source/address checks from complete two-dimensional Boolean execution in the [proof](https://github.com/jmbarrancoml/integer-mult-bounds/blob/898ff36fe2cd05f733de6b26c88a4c4741b06237/research/selected-source-packets/PROOF.md).

## Task and overlap

We refine `uniform-transfer-audit` to the directory/caller handoff from [PR2501](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2501), head `52a995b9d7f3e008c252770a5f47fde67a7cb37a`. We retain sixteen required dependencies without byte changes. We refreshed canonical main at 14:45 UTC: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4.

At 14:47 UTC, we searched 762 open PRs, 1,227 Discussions and 1,538 local records with complete pagination. We build on [PR2475](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2475), head `4d536232f392d7df44e716f6d6099f459e4d9035`, for conditional whole-call staging, and [PR2519](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2519), head `fe9ca26c8df754ccadbb3df89c721dad3b497b48`, for a separate one-buffer R439 adapter. We add physical directory production and common-view binding. At this check, ywz65 had an active PR2501 cost/ownership audit without a reported result. We record the scope, pins and credit in the [claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-18950583) and package TASK/SOURCES files.

## Validation

We passed the registered Python 3.12 source, complete-packet and optimized-control commands, plus metadata/pin and whitespace checks:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-source-packets --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-source-packets
```

- Exhaustive GL2/GL3 low coding; repeated and empty old prefixes; complete high-cube route/inverse checks through 6,561 matrices; fifteen rejection controls and 529-bit cardinalities.
- A complete 56-family, 435,456-bit COPY lifetime model with 55 XORs and one shared residual/child invocation.
- All 531,441 bit origins through a complete 81-high owner-route/directory/residual chain, including scratch cleanup and frozen-field preservation.
- Actual selected source keys, 128 COPY511 address columns, 16,517 fallback child calls and concrete selected consumer junctions.

We used CPython 3.12.13 on macOS arm64 and GL2 for the complete Boolean runs. We retain the selected GL64 Boolean payload, new Lean verification and independent human review as open checks. We record deterministic receipts in RESULT.json.

## Credit

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. We retain Apache-2.0 and credit OpenAI/Douglas Colkitt, the selected word/hosting lineage, commdata2338, Ross Richardson and the earlier raw-field/stream/residual contributions in NOTICE.md. We credit ywz65 for PR2475 and Ross Richardson for PR2519, preserving their separate scopes.

## Open next questions

Complete one selected `f=1` node by extending the request catalogue and joining the local words, idle calls, bridges and terminal exchange. Its residual children already fit the leaf implementation. The complete physical driver and its staging lifetimes remain the next interface; larger recursive return and directory-aware reserve admission follow. The package README and TASK.json give first steps and blockers.
